items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. The post Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lagos APC faults Pearse over comments on Tinubu’s academic records
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has faulted Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent media interviews concerning President Bola Tinubu’s academic history. The party’s spokesman, Seye Oladejo, said Pearse’s comments had revisited issues surrounding the President’s academic records, which he noted had been addressed through institutional confirmations and judicial proceedings. In a statement, the APC said it considered it necessary to respond to the comments, citing what it described as repeated claims about Tinubu’s academic qualifications. The party questioned Pearse’s account of his association with Chicago State University, stating that he reportedly worked at the institution between 1985 and 1990, while Tinubu’s academic records indicated that he attended the university between 1977 and 1979. It argued that Pearse’s period of association with the institution came several years after Tinubu’s reported graduation, raising questions about the basis of his comments on the President’s academic history. The APC also cited Chicago State University’s confirmation of Tinubu’s attendance and graduation in 1979. It recalled that the university’s Registrar, Caleb Westberg, testified under oath in October 2023 that the institution’s official records showed that Tinubu graduated on June 22, 1979, with a degree in Business Administration. According to the party, the confirmation was contained in official university records and sworn testimony presented during legal proceedings initiated by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. The APC maintained that discussions about the President’s academic history should take account of the university’s official records and relevant judicial proceedings. It also noted that legal challenges relating to Tinubu’s election had been determined by the courts, urging public commentators to focus on issues affecting Nigerians rather than repeatedly revisiting concluded disputes. The party said the 2027 general election should be centred on policy ideas, governance performance and the choices of the electorate. It urged Pearse to direct his contributions to national development and issues of public interest. The post Lagos APC faults Pearse over comments on Tinubu’s academic records appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le magistrat Ambroise Nébié analyse les litiges liés à la résiliation des marchés publics dans son nouvel ouvrage
items.description: Le magistrat Ambroise Nébié a présenté et dédicacé, le 19 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, son ouvrage intitulé « Le contentieux de la résiliation des contrats de la commande publique ». À travers cette publication, l’auteur entend éclairer les lecteurs sur le traitement des conflits liés à la rupture des contrats de la commande publique devant le juge administratif. Le choix de ce thème s’explique par l’importance de la commande publique dans le secteur économique. Selon l’auteur, les achats publics occupent une place majeure dans le fonctionnement de l’économie et génèrent des litiges qui nécessitent des réponses juridiques adaptées. « La commande publique occupe une grande partie dans notre secteur économique, en matière de litige sur les marchés publics la résiliation en fait partie », a déclaré Ambroise Nébié. Dans son ouvrage, l’auteur examine les différentes voies de recours ouvertes aux titulaires des marchés publics dont les contrats ont été résiliés. Il s’intéresse également aux arguments juridiques que ces derniers peuvent présenter devant le juge pour défendre leurs intérêts, ainsi qu’aux mécanismes utilisés par le juge administratif pour trancher les différends. Centré sur les décisions de justice, l’ouvrage analyse les différentes jurisprudences rendues par le juge en matière de résiliation des contrats. L’auteur adopte une double démarche descriptive et critique. Il ne se contente pas de présenter les décisions de justice, mais propose également une appréciation de celles-ci afin de faire ressortir les solutions retenues et les perspectives possibles. Cette démarche permet ainsi aux lecteurs de mieux comprendre comment les litiges liés à la résiliation des contrats de la commande publique sont examinés et résolus devant le juge administratif. L’ouvrage constitue notamment une source d’éclairage pour les avocats, les magistrats et les étudiants en droit. Magistrat de formation, Ambroise Nébié a exercé dans plusieurs juridictions administratives. Il a notamment servi au Tribunal administratif de Bobo-Dioulasso, puis à la Cour administrative d’appel de Ouagadougou. Depuis mai 2024, il exerce au Conseil d’État en qualité de commissaire du gouvernement adjoint. L’ouvrage est disponible à Ouagadougou à la Librairie universitaire, à la Librairie Jacket et à la Librairie Mercury, au prix de 7 000 F CFA. Grâce Kabré/Bazié Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le magistrat Ambroise Nébié analyse les litiges liés à la résiliation des marchés publics dans son nouvel ouvrage est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Kloto : Autorités coutumières et administratives mobilisées pour la reconnaissance des cheffes traditionnelles
items.description: Kpalimé, 20 nov. (ATOP) – Plus d’une centaine de chefs traditionnels, de reines mères du grand Kloto, des préfets et de maires ont pris part, le jeudi 19 novembre à Kpalimé, à une rencontre de renforcement des capacités consacrée à la reconnaissance institutionnelle des cheffes traditionnelles et à leur participation à la gouvernance locale. Initiée par l’ONG Alafia, avec l’appui financier de la Coopération allemande (GIZ), cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Nyonufia – Émergence des femmes dans les instances de gouvernance locale », mis en œuvre par l’ONG Alafia en consortium avec l’ONG Alafia Jeune. Elle vise à obtenir la reconnaissance institutionnelle des cheffes traditionnelles par les autorités administratives locales et à favoriser leur intégration, aux côtés des chefs traditionnels, dans les dispositifs de gouvernance locale du Grand Kloto. Il s’agit également de renforcer le dialogue entre les autorités coutumières et administratives des préfectures de Kloto, Kpélé, Danyi et Agou, afin de favoriser la reconnaissance et l’application des engagements coutumiers en faveur d’une participation équitable des femmes et des hommes à la gouvernance locale. La rencontre a aussi permis de présenter aux préfets et aux maires les engagements formalisés ainsi que les attentes des chefferies masculines et féminines en matière de reconnaissance institutionnelle et de collaboration. Les travaux ont porté, entre autres, sur la présentation des engagements coutumiers formalisés, les modalités pratiques de collaboration entre chefs traditionnels et cheffes traditionnelles, ainsi que la décision commune de référence. Le préfet de Kloto, Fiawofia Doagbodji Kodjo, a souligné que cette initiative s’inscrit dans la dynamique de renforcement de la gouvernance locale inclusive portée par le Président du Conseil et son gouvernement. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité des autorités administratives à accompagner les initiatives visant la promotion des droits et devoirs des reines mères et une gestion participative des communautés. Il a également invité les chefs traditionnels à accorder une place importante aux reines mères dans la gestion des affaires coutumières, dans l’intérêt de tous. La directrice exécutive de l’ONG Alafia, Mme Tatey Adzoavi Nyuito, a indiqué que cette rencontre fait suite à plusieurs séances d’information et de sensibilisation organisées à l’endroit des chefs traditionnels sur les droits, les devoirs et les rôles des reines mères. Elle a salué leur engagement en faveur de la reconnaissance et de l’exercice effectif des responsabilités de ces dernières. Elle a également annoncé un suivi des recommandations issues des échanges afin de veiller à leur mise en application. Mme Tatey a exhorté les femmes et les reines mères à poursuivre leur engagement pour une égalité effective entre les femmes et les hommes dans les domaines social, culturel et professionnel. La présidente des reines mères du Kloto, Mama Sikavi, a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux organisateurs pour cette initiative qui contribue à faire reconnaître et à valoriser le rôle des reines mères aux côtés des chefs traditionnels dans la gestion des collectivités locales. Elle a invité les autorités à œuvrer davantage pour une parité effective entre les femmes et les hommes dans les différentes sphères sociales, politiques et administratives, au service de l’intérêt général. Il convient de souligner que l’intronisation des reines mères, communément appelées « Mama », constitue une ancienne institution coutumière dans le Grand Kloto. Cette tradition, profondément ancrée dans les pratiques socioculturelles de la région, concerne les quatre préfectures : Agou, Danyi, Kloto et Kpélé. La reconnaissance institutionnelle de ces femmes vise ainsi à consolider leur rôle et leurs responsabilités dans la gestion des affaires coutumières et la gouvernance locale. ATOP/KAT/SED

Deputy Health Minister warns against examination malpractice in nursing schools
items.description: The Deputy Minister of Health, Professor Dr Grace Ayensu-Danquah, has cautioned health training institutions against examination malpractice, warning that graduating unqualified nurses and other health professionals could put patients’ lives at risk. She stressed that nurses and medical professionals must be properly trained, assessed and certified to ensure they possess the knowledge and skills required to deliver safe and effective healthcare. Prof. Ayensu-Danquah gave the warning during a working visit to selected health training institutions at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital in Accra. The institutions visited included the School of Public Health, School of Hygiene, Nursing and Midwifery Training College, and the School of Peri-Operative and Critical Care Nursing. During engagements with school authorities and staff, she expressed concern about examination malpractice, noting that health professionals were entrusted with the lives of patients, often at their most vulnerable moments. “Let us really graduate them or move them when they are really qualified. After they have done the examination, let us ensure that they have really passed and that they know the basics so that when they get out and are taking care of us, they are doing the right thing,” she said. She urged the institutions to maintain high academic and professional standards in the training and assessment of students. The Deputy Minister also called on healthcare professionals to show empathy and compassion towards patients, while acknowledging the pressure they face due to staff shortages and heavy workloads. She said the visit had offered the Ministry an opportunity to understand some of the challenges confronting the institutions, including inadequate infrastructure, shortages of teaching personnel and logistical constraints. On logistics, Prof. Ayensu-Danquah disclosed that the Ministry was working to provide pickup trucks to health training institutions to support their operations, with plans to address their demand for buses at a later stage. She said the Ministry was also assessing the staffing needs of the institutions to identify areas where personnel could be redistributed or additional staff recruited. The exercise would also consider ways to strengthen the capacity of existing staff through further training. The Deputy Minister further revealed that applications had opened for PhD programmes for staff of nursing training institutions as part of efforts to improve the academic and professional capacity of tutors. She added that the establishment of specialised nursing schools was among the measures being pursued to address the backlog of unemployed nurses while equipping them with advanced skills to respond to emerging healthcare needs. Prof. Ayensu-Danquah assured the institutions that concerns raised during the engagements would be considered for further deliberation and appropriate interventions.

items.title: Moffy, Gasmilla revisit Ga vibe with new single ‘Seaman Jorley’
items.description: Ghanaian musician Moffy has released a new single, Seaman Jorley , featuring Ga music and Azonto legend Gasmilla, in a creative blend of traditional Ga sounds and contemporary musical influences. The song combines Ga Pop, Afro Fusion and Three-Step rhythms to explore love, insecurity, heartbreak and the emotional baggage that can affect relationships. Inspired by the classic Ga Jama song of the same name, which tells the story of a seaman longing for his lover abroad, Moffy reimagines the familiar narrative through a modern relationship experience. In the new interpretation, he recounts how unresolved emotional experiences and past disappointments led him to suspect that his former lover was cheating on him over the phone. However, whether his suspicions were justified or driven by insecurity remains unanswered, leaving him caught in a cycle of doubt and unanswered questions. Listen here: rainlabs.lnk.to/SEAMANJORLEY Gasmilla adds another dimension to the story, reflecting on how painful past relationships made him build emotional walls around himself. Expecting his new partner to hurt him as others had done, he unknowingly becomes the source of her pain, reinforcing the idea that people who have experienced hurt can sometimes pass that pain on to others. Through the two perspectives, Seaman Jorley examines how unresolved trauma, mistrust and fear can shape people’s decisions and ultimately damage relationships. The production brings together Insvne Auggie, KQ THE ARTIST and Nii Quaye, who combine the song’s nostalgic Ga musical influence with contemporary rhythms. By drawing on a familiar Ga Jama composition while introducing modern sounds and relationship themes, Moffy seeks to connect a piece of Ga musical heritage with the experiences of a new generation of listeners. Beyond its danceable rhythms, Seaman Jorley tells a story about love, emotional vulnerability and the unanswered questions that sometimes remain after relationships come to an end.

items.title: Art Museums Shouldn’t Need Taylor Swift
items.description: When the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, shared Tuesday that it would mount an exhibition of Taylor Swift costumes, instruments, and other objects next year, the public response seemed to fall into two camps. Swifties were thrilled, and art purists criticized the museum for succumbing to visitor bait. But really, neither scorn nor celebration is the right response to a show that one of the museum’s curators describes as representing “a remarkable musical journey across genres over the last 20 years.” A 156-year-old institution raiding a pop star’s closet should be seen for what it is: a cry for help. The show does not entirely flout museum norms. The MFA’s collection includes fashion and musical instruments. Art institutions have examined celebrity wardrobes in the past (see the landmark David Bowie exhibition that traveled around the world), and museums frequently highlight living visual artists and designers—sometimes, as in the Met’s recent plans for a John Galliano exhibit, to their peril. Why not Swift? She seems to have conquered nearly every other corner of the culture. An illustration of her range: She both is the subject of university courses and once had her own special-edition ketchup bottle . Perhaps to her fans, her rightful place in history is alongside the old masters and the Impressionists. Step back, and you can see why there’s hype for the show, but it’s still a mismatch. The museum sector has been having a hard time lately, making this type of pop-culture play understandably tempting. But after the MFA laid off 33 employees, including curators of Islamic art, Native American art, and fashion arts, earlier this year, the show choice looks more than a little desperate. Although Taylor Swift’s sartorial history may be worthy of serious scholarly analysis—mass culture certainly has a place in art museums, which should help us understand the visual world writ large—tackling the subject of a living celebrity at the height of her fame renders hagiography practically a foregone conclusion. The MFA is not even pretending otherwise: One staffer made a point of extending a special welcome to Swifties in the announcement. The exhibition will very likely serve as an advertisement for a star who needs no such boost in the hopes that the museum can lure more visitors, who will be paying $40 each to look at her stuff. For an institution that contains one of the finest art collections in the world, the decision belies a deep insecurity. When I saw the news, I had an urge to shout at the MFA like it’s a friend of mine who’s in a toxic relationship: You don’t need her, buddy! You’re great! The tendency to star-cast museum shows does not necessarily lead to bad or uninteresting results. These exhibitions have historically taken one of two approaches: In one, the celebrity might be drafted to curate an exhibition (which must be a tad annoying to the curators who might’ve gone through the trouble of getting a degree to do that). In the other, the museum assembles an exhibit of the celebrity’s belongings or artistic ephemera. The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, which went through its own round of layoffs last year, recently opened an exhibition doing a bit of both. The institution is currently showcasing nearly 150 works from the art collection of the BTS member RM, and the show is co-curated by the K-pop star himself. Some celebrity-infused endeavors have succeeded, such as the acclaimed Bowie show or a well-liked exhibition of Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz’s collection that the Brooklyn Museum organized. Others, such as Björk at the Museum of Modern Art in 2015 or the Pablo Picasso show co-curated by Hannah Gadsby at the Brooklyn Museum in 2023, flopped with critics but drew crowds, presumably fulfilling their purpose. If it’s not clear, I am neither a Swiftie nor a K-pop stan, which may disqualify me from a conversation for the truly devout. That said, having lived in Seoul, I am a real admirer of Korean art and would accept almost any strategy to show more Americans Kim Whanki’s moving abstractions or Chang Ucchin’s charming pastoral scenes. And the RM exhibit has done that, breaking museum records. Even so, something feels off to me. Such shows can raise ethical questions—displaying any person’s art collection, for example, can inflate its value—but more than that, they can hurt a museum’s credibility. A doctor would not hand her sutures over to Beyoncé just because her surgery numbers are down, nor would a losing football team throw Justin Bieber on the field because he might bring in some new fans. The stakes are different in museums, but these places shape history, care for cultural heritage, and at their core, are meant to challenge and educate visitors. The stakes of swapping in celebrities for curators and their paraphernalia for objects are not exactly low either. Many museums have struggled to rebound after the pandemic changed visitor habits and have not found their way in a world that seems to become more digital by the day. They’ve faced alternating allegations of being overly woke and being complicit in colonialism. And although they are widely trusted , museums remain one of the few places that spark anxiety among would-be visitors over not having done their homework. No one hesitates to go to a concert because they didn’t study music theory. Perhaps you cannot blame the MFA or SFMOMA for looking to the crowd-pleaser to pad the numbers. It’s easy. Too easy. Paying the bills, for the MFA, might mean loosening up a bit—not everyone wants to parse the stories told by an intricate Japanese folding screen or sit long enough with a Mondrian to see how it’s more than just a colorful grid. But museums’ usual purview holds plenty of mass appeal as is. In a way, the situation parallels how museums tap certain go-to artists and genres to woo the public: Yayoi Kusama with her impossibly photogenic mirrors; Impressionists with their coffee-table-book-ready textural landscapes; the treasures of ancient Egypt . The best museums don’t just give people what they want, though; they teach us how to look, and empower us to find aesthetic joy for ourselves. More compelling than celebrity shows are efforts to pull new audiences that confidently lean into what museums already do. Many have started opening for late-night hours, becoming the kinds of third places so many communities are short on. The Museum of Vancouver recently went the Brené Brown route and highlighted its vulnerability, giving “austerity tours” that showed the toll of low funding. (Kind of depressing—but it definitely got people talking.) The National Gallery of Art, meanwhile, has a curator translating old objects into the language of Gen Z on social media; the institution is also inviting people in for “Finding Awe” sessions that train visitors to look closely and patiently at objects. During a recent session, a visitor commented that after seeing so much AI content, noticing the imperfections of an Agnes Martin canvas felt rewarding. Museums can make themselves relevant to contemporary viewers by finding the relatable and the universal in the art they’re trusted with stewarding, not borrowing relevance in the shape of a celebrity’s dress. A common justification for more populist shows goes something like: The exhibition gets visitors in the door. After that, they might encounter something that could spark a lifelong interest in art . I don’t love the way this logic characterizes art like a bad-tasting pill that must go down coated in peanut butter. The art museum’s job, if nothing else, is to convince us that the art is the peanut butter. So if there must be a Swift show, I hope the thinking proves true. During the Swift exhibit’s run, the MFA will also, at one point, be hosting a show of paintings by Mary Cassatt , the only American to exhibit with the French Impressionists. Cassatt had an intimate and intentional way of capturing women’s experiences in a male-dominated world. Sound familiar? Maybe some of those visiting Swifties will enter their Cassatt era next. *Illustration sources: Brooke Sutton / Getty; Ethan Miller / ACMA / Getty; iStock / Getty; Kevin Mazur / Getty; Kevin Winter / Getty; TAS24 / Getty; Tibrina Hobson / Getty; Tommaso Boddi / Wire Image / Getty.

items.title: We still have not received our per diems – Black Challenge players appeal to gov’t after historic World Cup feat
items.description: Ghana’s Black Challenge have appealed to the government, particularly the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, to provide the team with the necessary support following their historic qualification for the semi-finals of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup. The Black Challenge made history on Thursday after recording a 2-0 victory over Egypt to book their place in the last four of the competition for the first time. The players received a $10,000 cash reward from National Paralympic Committee (NPC) President Samson Deen for reaching the last eight, with each player receiving approximately $650. The aforementioned amount is currently being processed as a second reward from NPC President Deen after the semi-final qualification. However, the players feel neglected by Sports Minister Kofi Adams, particularly following their historic achievement. Star player Mubarik Mohammed, who has scored six goals at the tournament, has appealed to the government and the Ministry to give the team the attention and support they deserve. “Our President, Samson Deen, is doing his part by giving us something as motivation, but I want to plead with our leaders because we have still not heard anything, especially from the Ministry of Sports and Recreation led by Kofi Adams. “We know he has us at heart. We had a conversation with him before coming here, so we are pleading with him. We want to see some action from them because we are doing our part representing the motherland. “We have still not received our per diems from the Ministry, nor have we received any update regarding what we have achieved. I am pleading with our leaders to attend to us as we move into the semi-finals, as that will serve as a huge motivation for us,” he said. Information available to JoySports indicates that the outstanding per diem allocation amounts to $18,000, calculated at $100 per day for each of the 15 players over 12 days. Ghana will face Turkey in the semi-finals on Saturday at 1:30 am Ghana time, with the Black Challenge hoping to secure a historic place in the final.

items.description: La Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) a fermé cinq boutiques dans des marchés à Ouagadougou, au cours d'une opération, ce vendredi novembre 2026. Le ministère du Commerce est toujours dans sa dynamique de lutter contre l'augmentation anarchique des prix des produits de grande consommation au Burkina Faso. Dans cette optique, sa structure, la Brigade mobile de contrôle économique et de la répression des fraudes (BMCRF) a poursuivi des opérations de contrôle dans les quartiers aux alentours des marchés de Sankar Yaaré, Dapoya et 10 Yaar. Au total, « cinq boutiques de produits de grande consommation ont été fermées pour des infractions de pratiques de prix illicites, défaut d’affichage des tarifs, non-respect des conditions d’exercice, vente de marchandises périmées », informe la BMCRF qui souligne que les « commerçants véreux ont été réquisitionnés pour des travaux d’intérêt général ». Les contacts utiles en vue de joindre ses équipes dont « 80 00 11 84 / 80 00 11 85 / 80 00 11 86 » ont été disponibilisés. items.title: African ministers warn against empty promises at COP31, demand delivery of climate finance
items.description: African ministers have mounted a united call for developed countries to honour their climate finance commitments, warning that failure to deliver promised resources will undermine the implementation of the Paris Agreement and deepen the vulnerability of millions of people across the continent. At a press conference in Antalya, Türkiye, on the final day of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), ministers from Ghana, Kenya, Zambia, Senegal and Sierra Leone said Africa would not accept another climate outcome built on declarations without adequate financial support. Representing 54 African countries, Ghana’s Minister of Environment, Science and Technology, Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, said the continent had come to the negotiations to demand what was rightfully due to its people, rather than appeal for assistance. She accused developed countries of creating barriers to accessing climate finance through increasingly restrictive conditions, shifting goalposts and delays in delivering promised resources. “We’re here on behalf of over a billion people who are supposed to be the custodians of this framework, but it seems we’ve been excluded, not through technicalities, but through inaccessible finance, the use of shifting goalposts and non-delivery of promises,” she said. The ministers insisted that the final COP31 outcome must prioritise adaptation finance, operationalise commitments to triple adaptation funding and establish clear mechanisms for tracking financial delivery. Africa had arrived at COP31 seeking a credible pathway towards tripling adaptation finance, but the proposal was initially left out of the official agenda. The ministers said African negotiators had nevertheless sustained pressure across the various negotiation tracks to secure progress on the issue. They cited the significant gap between available adaptation resources and the financial requirements of developing countries, with estimates of adaptation finance needs reaching approximately US$35 billion annually by 2050. The African position is also pushing for at least US$120 billion annually by 2035 as an initial benchmark in advancing the tripling of adaptation finance. However, the ministers warned that financial targets without clear implementation arrangements, timelines and accountability mechanisms would do little to address the continent’s growing climate vulnerabilities. They are therefore demanding an agreed baseline, measurable milestones, public tracking and a clear delivery plan to ensure that commitments translate into accessible and predictable funding. These are lives lost, and livelihoods destroyed Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings said Africa’s position was rooted in the lived experiences of communities already suffering the consequences of climate change. She argued that the Paris Agreement represented a collective commitment to pursue a different development pathway, with developed countries expected to support developing economies in adapting to climate impacts and transitioning towards sustainable development. However, she expressed concern that some developed countries appeared unwilling to honour their financial obligations. “We cannot keep changing the agreement to fit what developed countries want. Then there is no purpose in having an agreement if we keep shifting the goalposts,” she said. She called for a strong signal from developed countries that existing commitments would be respected, insisting that African countries had also demonstrated commitment to the global climate framework. Kenya’s Cabinet Secretary for Environment, Climate Change and Forestry, Dr. Deborah Mlongo Barasa, highlighted the devastating consequences of climate change across African communities, including food and water insecurity, declining agricultural production, livestock losses and humanitarian emergencies. She cited the experiences of farmers recording reduced harvests, pastoralists losing livestock and communities whose health and education facilities have been disrupted by flooding. In some affected areas, submerged schools have prevented children from accessing education, while health facilities face challenges delivering essential services, including immunisation. She said adaptation, loss and damage financing were critical to ensuring that affected communities received the resources needed to recover and build resilience. The minister also highlighted Africa’s energy access challenge, noting that more than 600 million people on the continent still lack access to electricity. She argued that the global energy transition must therefore be supported with adequate resources to expand access while enabling countries to pursue sustainable development. Africa demands a just transition Minister of Green Economy and Environment in Zambia, Gilbert Siame, also called for a just transition framework that recognises Africa’s development priorities and ensures that the continent benefits from the global shift towards cleaner energy. He stressed that Africa must not be burdened with transition requirements that undermine employment, economic growth and the development of its natural resources. The continent is particularly concerned about ensuring fair terms for the extraction and processing of critical minerals needed for the global energy transition. The ministers want African countries to move beyond supplying raw materials to the global market and develop the capacity to process and utilise these resources locally. They said a credible transition must protect workers and communities, create economic opportunities and be supported by adequate finance, technology transfer and capacity building. They also called on the COP31 Presidency and negotiating parties to ensure that political cover decisions do not replace concrete agreements emerging from the formal negotiation tracks. Africa wants adaptation finance and the climate finance work programme to remain central to the final outcome, with measurable and time-bound commitments. The ministers said the continent remained ready to work constructively with the COP Presidency and other parties towards an ambitious and credible agreement. However, they warned that the failure to honour existing commitments would further erode trust in the multilateral climate process. For Africa, they said, the test of COP31 is not simply the declarations adopted at the conference, but whether the commitments translate into resources that protect lives, sustain livelihoods and support the continent’s development.

items.title: Nuit de la philanthropie : un trophée sur fond d’urgence humanitaire.
items.description: © Internet Le directeur national du Développement social a reçu une distinction samedi 14 novembre à Bamako, lors de la 12e Nuit de la philanthropie. Son intervention a ramené la cérémonie à une urgence du moment : l’accueil des personnes refoulées de Guinée. Ibrahima Abba Sangaré connaissait la Nuit de la philanthropie pour y avoir remis des trophées. Cette année, c’est lui qui en a reçu un. Originaire de Goundam, dans la région de Tombouctou, le directeur national du Développement social a été distingué au Centre international de conférences de Bamako, devant les associations et partenaires réunis pour la soirée. L’intéressé a choisi de partager cet hommage avec ses anciens collègues. Il a notamment évoqué Modibo Diallo, ancien directeur national du Développement social, qui l’avait accompagné à ses débuts. « C’est lui qui a guidé mes premiers pas au niveau du ministère. J’ai suivi ses traces jusqu’à m’asseoir sur sa chaise », a-t-il raconté, suscitant les rires dans la salle. Son parcours l’a conduit dans les services régionaux du développement social, puis à la direction nationale, dont il était déjà l’adjoint en 2016. Il en est aujourd’hui le directeur. Dans ses fonctions, il intervient notamment dans la coordination de l’assistance aux personnes déplacées et aux populations touchées par les crises. La situation des personnes arrivées de Guinée a occupé une place dans son intervention. Sangaré a remercié les associations, les bénévoles et les entreprises mobilisés pour leur prise en charge. Parmi les contributions évoquées figure celle de 10 millions de francs CFA remise le 9 novembre par Moov Africa Malitel au ministère de la Santé et du Développement social. La BNDA avait apporté 50 millions de francs CFA lors de la même cérémonie. Quelques jours auparavant, le ministère avait évalué à près de 228 millions de francs CFA son plan d’urgence pour l’hébergement, l’alimentation, la santé, la protection et le transport des personnes concernées. Ce contexte donnait une résonance particulière aux appels à la solidarité lancés samedi au CICB. Sangaré a également salué le travail de l’Association Philanthropie, organisatrice de la soirée, et celui des organisations engagées durant le Mois de la solidarité. À ses yeux, la distinction reçue reconnaît aussi le travail collectif accompli par les agents sociaux et leurs partenaires.

items.title: Doufelgou : un nouveau marché bétail inauguré à Défalé
items.description: Niamtougou, 20 nov. (ATOP) – Un nouveau marché à bétail a été inauguré le jeudi 19 novembre à Défalé, dans la commune Doufelgou 2. Cette infrastructure vise à dynamiser la filière agropastorale et à améliorer les conditions de commercialisation du cheptel. Elle a été réalisée grâce au financement de la Société nationale de financement routier (SONAFIR), à hauteur de 16.750.000 F CFA. Cet ouvrage entend offrir aux acteurs de la filière un cadre sécurisé, fonctionnel et mieux organisé pour les transactions commerciales. Erigé sur une emprise de 40 mètres de long sur 23 mètres de large, l’ouvrage comprend deux compartiments destinés au regroupement des bovins, reliés à un couloir d’acheminement conduisant directement à l’aire d’embarquement. Deux hangars ont également été aménagés sur le site. Le premier est destiné à accueillir les petits ruminants, notamment les moutons et les chèvres, tandis que le second servira d’abri aux vendeurs et aux acheteurs. Le préfet de Doufelgou, colonel Aziaba Ayi Sessi, a indiqué que cette infrastructure moderne et sécurisée contribuera à dynamiser les filières agricoles et pastorales, à soutenir les initiatives des jeunes et des femmes, à accroître les recettes communales et à favoriser le développement d’activités connexes, notamment le commerce, le transport et la restauration. Il a exprimé le souhait que ce marché devienne un véritable espace de paix, de prospérité et de solidarité. Pour sa part, le maire de Doufelgou 2, Mme Koubonou Atiota Touni, a souligné que cette infrastructure va au-delà de simples enclos et hangars. Elle constitue, selon elle, un instrument de dignité pour les éleveurs, qui pourront désormais effectuer directement leurs transactions sans nécessairement recourir à des intermédiaires. Mme Koubonou a relevé que ce marché représente un levier de mobilisation des recettes communales et un cadre de cohésion sociale, de brassage et d’échanges entre les différents acteurs de divers horizons. Le maire a invité les populations et les éleveurs à préserver l’infrastructure, à veiller à la vaccination des animaux afin de prévenir les maladies et de protéger la santé humaine. Elle s’est engagée, avec le comité de gestion, à assurer une administration durable et transparente du marché afin d’en faire un véritable pôle de développement économique. Un comité de gestion, dirigé par M. Amadou Hassan, a été mis en place pour coordonner le bon déroulement des activités du marché. ATOP/SG/TAL/BA

items.title: Israël : les Palestiniens victimes d'une vague d'agressions sur fond de tensions politiques
items.description: Les citoyens palestiniens d' Israel denoncent une serie d'agressions survenues les 18 et 19 novembre, dans un climat politique tendu depuis les elections legislatives d'octobre. Dans le village d'Ed-Dahi, pres d'Afula, une mosquee a ete incendiee dans la nuit du 18 au 19 novembre. Selon son imam, Khaled Zoabi, trois individus ont brise une vitre et lance des cocktails Molotov dans le bâtiment. Des inscriptions racistes, dont le mot « vengeance », ont ete decouvertes a proximite. Quelques heures auparavant, huit personnes avaient ete blessees a Kafr Qasim, dans le centre du pays, apres avoir ete percutees par une voiture a quatre endroits differents. Parmi elles figuraient des femmes sortant d'un mariage. Un suspect a ete interpelle. La police examine le caractere intentionnel des faits et a indique qu'il avait ete teste positif aux stupefiants. a Karmiel, des slogans hostiles aux Arabes ont egalement ete peints sur des immeubles. Netanyahou le pyromane Ces violences surviennent apres la percee electorale des partis arabes, qui ont obtenu 19 sieges a la Knesset lors du scrutin du 27 octobre. Prive de majorite, Benjamin Netanyahou accuse regulierement ces formations de soutenir le terrorisme, tandis que son parti denonce, sans preuves etablies, des elections « volees ». Certains de ses allies d'extreme droite reclament l'annulation des resultats ou l'arrestation de responsables politiques arabes. Les elus palestiniens y voient une campagne de stigmatisation. Ahmad Tibi tient le Premier ministre pour politiquement responsable du climat hostile, tandis que Youssef Jabareen redoute de nouvelles agressions. Des personnalites de l'opposition juive, notamment Yaïr Lapid et Yaïr Golan, ont egalement condamne l'incendie de la mosquee. Aucun lien direct entre ces attaques et les declarations de Netanyahou n'a ete etabli par les enqueteurs. Mais pour les citoyens palestiniens, qui representent plus d'un cinquieme de la population israelienne, cette succession d'incidents ravive les inquietudes concernant leur securite et leur place dans la vie politique du pays.

items.title: European leaders urge Russia to halt winter energy attacks
items.description: …Back ceasefire, security guarantees for Ukraine By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine have called on Russia to suspend attacks on energy facilities throughout the winter, describing an energy truce as a first step towards ending hostilities in Ukraine. The leaders also called for a ceasefire to facilitate food exports through the Black Sea, stressing that safe passage for ships was critical to global food security. The position was contained in a joint statement shared by the German Embassy in Nigeria on Friday, following a meeting in Berlin on Thursday involving Ukraine, the United States and members of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries supporting Ukraine. The leaders condemned what they described as an escalation in Russian missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian civilians and civilian infrastructure, while expressing condolences to the families of victims. They reaffirmed their solidarity with Ukraine and its right to defend itself against Russia’s invasion, insisting that continued attacks would not weaken their support for Kyiv. The statement said the countries would work with other partners to provide Ukraine with additional missile defence systems before winter, particularly those capable of intercepting ballistic missiles to protect civilians and critical infrastructure. The leaders also backed direct talks between Ukraine and Russia, with the participation of the United States and European countries, and welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s willingness to accept an immediate ceasefire and engage in meaningful negotiations. They, however, insisted that any peace agreement must respect Ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and right to determine its security arrangements and alliances. According to the statement, proposals concerning the European Union or NATO would require the consent of their respective members. The leaders further called for legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect. The proposed arrangements include a US-led mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire and a European-led multinational force supported by the United States. Other measures could include continued military, financial and technical assistance to Ukraine, as well as a legally binding commitment, subject to national procedures, to take steps to restore peace and security if Russia launches another armed attack. On military assistance, the leaders reaffirmed a pledge by NATO allies to provide €70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training in 2026, with at least the same level of support in 2027. They also said the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan would provide €90 billion in military and financial assistance by the end of 2027. The countries pledged to work with Ukraine on agreed reforms, particularly strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption. On sanctions, the leaders agreed to pursue additional measures targeting Russian oil and gas revenues, cryptocurrency and illicit financial flows. They also pledged to disrupt Russia’s military industry and restrict the activities of its shadow fleet, which they said Moscow uses to evade international sanctions. The statement further maintained that Russian sovereign assets would remain frozen until Moscow ends the war and compensates Ukraine for the damage caused. The leaders also condemned alleged Russian acts of sabotage, information operations and cyberattacks across Europe, describing them as attempts to undermine international support for Ukraine. They warned that such actions would not deter their commitment to Ukraine but would strengthen their resolve to bolster the security of Ukraine, Europe and NATO. The statement said, “As a first step towards a cessation of hostilities, the leaders called on Russia to agree to an energy ceasefire for the duration of the winter.” It added that international borders must not be changed by force and that Ukraine’s sovereign right to choose its security arrangements and alliances must be fully respected. items.title: Le Bureau du citoyen des Lacs 3 présenté aux populations de Gbodjomé
items.description: Aného, 20 nov. (ATOP) – Le Bureau du citoyen (BDC) de la commune Lacs 3 a été présenté, le mercredi 18 novembre, aux populations du canton de Gbodjomé. Cette cérémonie a permis de faire connaître aux populations les missions, les attributions et le fonctionnement de cette nouvelle structure de participation citoyenne. Le Bureau est dirigé par M. Agbekoué Koffi, en qualité de coordonnateur. Il est assisté de Mme Bocna Rebécca, rapporteure. Le bureau du citoyen sert de trait d’union entre les élus locaux et les citoyens, dans une dynamique de gouvernance participative. Conçu comme un cadre d’écoute, d’expression et de dialogue, il offre aux habitants un espace où ils peuvent faire entendre leurs voix, exposer leurs préoccupations, formuler des propositions ou solliciter des orientations sur les questions liées à la gestion de leur commune. Cet instrument va faciliter les échanges entre les citoyens et les responsables municipaux, tout en contribuant à la recherche de solutions aux difficultés rencontrées par les populations, notamment à travers le dialogue et la médiation. Au-delà de sa fonction d’écoute, cette structure se veut également un instrument de promotion de la transparence, de la redevabilité et de la bonne gouvernance locale. Elle doit permettre aux administrés de mieux comprendre les actions de la municipalité, de faire part de leurs attentes et de participer davantage aux réflexions sur les politiques et initiatives de développement communal. La rencontre s’est déroulée en présence du maire des Lacs 3, Anani Oleassan, et du député Jonas Drafoé. ATOP/AAK/BA/BV

items.title: Gombe APC Chairman, Campaign DG flown to Abuja after accident
items.description: …Two persons died in Tuesday’s crash By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have been transferred to an undisclosed hospital in Abuja for further medical attention following a road accident that claimed two lives in the state. The two party chieftains were reportedly transferred on Thursday from the Federal Teaching Hospital (FTH), Gombe, where they had been receiving treatment since the accident. Vanguard gathered during a visit to the hospital on Friday that their transfer was not necessarily due to any lack of capacity at the Federal Teaching Hospital to manage their medical conditions, but was largely intended to provide them with a more conducive environment for treatment, privacy and adequate rest. Sources familiar with the development, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the continuous influx of politicians, party supporters and other sympathisers seeking to visit the injured APC leaders had made it difficult for them to enjoy the privacy and tranquillity required for their recovery. According to the sources, their transfer was aimed at enabling them to concentrate on their treatment without the distractions associated with frequent visits. Ndus and Hassan were involved in the accident on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of Gombe State. The crash reportedly claimed two lives, while the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were subsequently rushed to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, for medical attention. Their transfer to Abuja is expected to allow them to continue their treatment in a more private environment. items.title: Encadrement des loyers : le Parlement français prolonge de deux ans le dispositif contesté
items.description: Le vote survenu en soiree le 19 novembre a l'Assemblee nationale sauve in extremis le plafonnement des loyers, qui devait prendre fin le 24 novembre. Porte initialement par le depute socialiste Iñaki Echaniz pour le perenniser et l'etendre, le texte a ete recentre par le Senat sur une simple prolongation de deux ans, jusqu'en 2028, dans les zones deja concernees alors que le pays est frappe par le phenomene de « mal-logement » . 🌹 Journée socialiste à l’Assemblée : deux victoires ! ✅ Territoires zéro chômeur : pérennisé. ✅ Encadrement des loyers : adopté, malgré 6h d’obstruction du RN ! L’extrême droite a choisi les plus aisés. Nous, les Français. https://t.co/fxfNU2YBLj — Romain Eskenazi (@RomainEskenazi) November 19, 2026 Une seance houleuse et un recours gouvernemental Les debats se sont deroules dans un climat tendu. Face au depot de centaines de sous-amendements par le Rassemblement national (RN), le ministre du Logement Vincent Jeanbrun a invoque l'article, 44 alinea 2, de la Constitution pour ecarter ceux non examines en commission, denoncant une « obstruction ». Plusieurs groupes ont pointe l'inegalite de traitement par rapport a d'autres niches parlementaires. La deputee socialiste Sandrine Runel a denonce l'obstruction du RN et du centre macroniste et a reagit en declarant sur X : « Ce que nous demandons est simple : permettre aux locataires de ne pas avoir a choisir entre payer leur loyer et se nourrir ! » @guillaumekasba et ses alliés du @RNational_off s’acharnent contre les locataires en faisant de l’obstruction sur l’encadrement des loyers. Ce que nous demandons est simple : permettre aux locataires de ne pas avoir à choisir entre payer leur loyer et se nourrir ! — Sandrine Runel (@SandrineRunel) November 19, 2026 Cote opposition, Eddy Casterman (Identite et Libertes) a denonce « la grande tambouille » de la gauche et du gouvernement. Le dispositif, issu de la loi elan de 2018, s'applique a Paris, Lyon, Villeurbanne, Lille, Bordeaux, Montpellier, ainsi qu'a des communes de Seine-Saint-Denis, de l'agglomeration grenobloise et du Pays basque. Il fixe chaque annee, par arrete prefectoral, un loyer de reference selon le quartier, le nombre de pieces et l'epoque de construction. Le loyer de base ne peut depasser cette reference majoree de 20 %, sauf complement justifie. La Ville de Paris a salue une « victoire majeure », rappelant que pres de 3,2 millions d'euros de loyers indûment percus ont ete rembourses aux locataires depuis 2023. Les critiques persistent toutefois : economistes et Cour des comptes jugent les effets limites , avec une erosion de l'offre locative et un gain surtout pour les locataires deja en place. Aucune nouvelle commune, comme Marseille qui le reclame, ne pourra y entrer d'ici 2028.

items.title: France : de Villepin se lance dans la course à la présidentielle
items.description: L'ex-Premier ministre Dominique de Villepin a officialisé vendredi sa candidature à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 en France en se présentant comme une alternative aux partis responsables selon lui du « pourrissement » du pays. « Je suis candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 », a lancé lors d'une conférence de presse à Paris celui qui est surtout connu à l'étranger pour son discours à l'ONU portant le « non » français à la guerre américaine en Irak en 2003. L'élection présidentielle française se tiendra les 18 avril et 2 mai 2027. En campagne de fait depuis plusieurs mois, l'ancien ministre des Affaires étrangères (2002-2004) de Jacques Chirac plafonnait début novembre à 3% des intentions de vote. Ses détracteurs lui reprochent ses activités lucratives et conférences à l'étranger ces deux dernières décennies, notamment en Chine. De Villepin a réfuté tout conflit d'intérêts. Tout comme dans l'affaire des statuettes reçues lorsqu'il était ministre des Affaires étrangères, qu'il a depuis données au Quai d'Orsay. Né le 14 novembre 1953 à Rabat, Dominique de Villepin est entré dans la carrière diplomatique à sa sortie de l’École nationale d’administration (promotion Voltaire, 1980). Il a servi la France au Quai d’Orsay et à l’étranger avant d’exercer les plus hautes responsabilités de l’État. Il fut ainsi Directeur de cabinet d’Alain Juppé, ministre des Affaires étrangères (1993-1995), Secrétaire général de la présidence de la République auprès de Jacques Chirac (1995-2002), Ministre des Affaires étrangères (2002-2004), Ministre de l’Intérieur (2004-2005), et Premier ministre (2005-2007). Il est également Fondateur de La France Humaniste, un mouvement politique créé en juin 2025, et qui se réclame du gaullisme, de l'humanisme, de l'universalisme républicain et du souverainisme, en cherchant à se démarquer tant de La France insoumise que du Rassemblement national et de la continuité du macronisme. The post France : de Villepin se lance dans la course à la présidentielle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mining firms urged to create inclusive workplaces to boost women’s participation
items.description: The Gender Ministry has urged mining and transport companies to adopt inclusive workplace policies and provide career advancement opportunities, to increase women’s participation in Ghana’s traditionally male-dominated industries. Vera Kakari Badiako, the Director for Gender Equity at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, said deliberate efforts were needed to remove institutional barriers that prevented women from entering, remaining and advancing in the mining and heavy transport sectors. She said policies promoting gender equality must translate into practical opportunities, including fair recruitment, access to technical training, safe working environments, mentorship, and equal leadership opportunities. Madam Badiako made the call at the launch of the Empowering Women in Mining Transport Project, organised by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) (develoPPP), Scania West Africa, Reach for Change and Women in Mining Ghana. It was on the theme: “Accelerating Women’s Participation in Ghana’s Heavy Transport and Mining Industries through Skills Development and Strategic Partnerships.” She said data from the Ghana Chamber of Mines indicated that women constituted about 10 per cent of the workforce in the large-scale mining sector, with 14 per cent occupying senior positions and 21 per cent in professional roles. Although the figures showed some progress, they highlighted the need for sustained interventions to improve women’s representation, particularly in technical, operational and leadership positions, she said. Madam Badiako said the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121), provided a framework for addressing women’s under-representation, with a minimum representation target of 30 per cent by the end of 2026 and gender parity by 2034. She urged employers to regard compliance with the Act not merely as a statutory requirement but as an opportunity to strengthen institutional performance by expanding access to a wider pool of talent. She also encouraged women already working in the mining sector to mentor younger ones, share their experiences and support efforts to attract more females into the industry. Mr Richard Ashong, the Communications Superintendent of AngloGold Ashanti, said supportive workplace policies were essential to ensuring that women could combine their professional responsibilities with their personal and family needs. He said the company had introduced measures, including a Baby Care Centre launched in 2024, to enable nursing mothers to access their babies during work breaks. Other interventions included extending maternity leave from 12 to 16 weeks, with 20 weeks for mothers of twins or multiple births, providing specially designed workwear for female and pregnant employees, and making sanitary pads freely available at workplaces and washrooms. He said the company also invested in technical skills development through its Women in Industry Skills and Empowerment Programme under the Mines Youth Apprenticeship Training Programme. “In 2025, 42 women were enrolled in the programme, which offered training in mobile crane rigging, fabrication, auto mechanics, industrial mechanics and auto electricals.” Mr Ashong said the company remained committed to extending empowerment opportunities to women in its host communities through vocational training and apprenticeship initiatives. Mr Francois Lechat, the Managing Director of Scania West Africa, said the Project would provide women with professional driving skills, safety and defensive driving practices, vehicle familiarisation and operational training. He said the initiative would train 80 women as professional heavy-duty truck drivers, while another 200 would receive training in entrepreneurship, digital literacy, workplace safety, mining operations and sexual harassment prevention. He said the mining and transport industries offered significant employment opportunities and that equipping women with the necessary competencies would help address skills shortages and promote diversity. Mr Lechat said the objective was to move beyond training to creating sustainable career opportunities for women in the industry. He encouraged the participants to approach the programme with commitment and confidence, saying their success could inspire other women to consider careers in heavy transport and mining.

items.title: Haruna Iddrisu and NDC’s leadership future: Experience, political maturity and the national question
items.description: Political leadership is rarely the product of a single achievement, appointment or moment of public recognition. More often, it emerges through years of institutional engagement, exposure to complex national challenges, difficult political decisions and the gradual development of the judgement required to manage competing interests. In a democratic society, these experiences provide an important basis for evaluating individuals who may aspire to the highest levels of public office. As Ghana’s political landscape evolves and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) looks towards its next phase of leadership, the political journey of Honourable Haruna Iddrisu, Minister for Education and Member of Parliament for Tamale South, offers an important subject for national reflection. Interestingly, he has been seen to avoid that discourse and interest, leaving his admirers and many other observers wondering. For nearly three decades, Haruna has occupied positions that have exposed him to the workings of political parties, Parliament and the executive arm of government. His progression from student leadership to national party organisation, parliamentary representation, ministerial appointments and opposition leadership provides a distinctive combination of political and administrative experience. The significance of this journey lies not merely in the number of positions he has occupied, but in the breadth of responsibilities, institutions and national development challenges he has encountered. This accumulated experience makes his political career relevant to the broader conversation about leadership renewal, institutional competence, and the future direction of the NDC. Haruna’s political development began with student leadership, particularly his presidency of the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) in 1996–1997. That experience provided an early foundation in advocacy, negotiation, political mobilization, and managing competing interests. His subsequent service as National Youth Organiser of the NDC between 2002 and 2010 placed him within the party’s organisational structures during an important period of political rebuilding and electoral competition. His election to Parliament in 2004 marked another stage in his development, introducing him to legislative responsibilities, national policy debates and the practical demands of democratic representation. Over the years, his parliamentary career has evolved from ordinary legislative participation to managing some of the most consequential responsibilities within Ghana’s parliamentary democracy. Perhaps the most distinctive aspect of Haruna’s public service is the diversity of his ministerial experience. Few political figures of his generation have served across portfolios as interconnected and nationally significant as Communications, Trade and Industry, Employment and Labour Relations, and Education. As Minister for Communications between 2009 and 2013, Haruna served during a period when Ghana’s telecommunications sector was undergoing substantial transformation. His tenure coincided with important regulatory and technological developments, including mobile number portability, SIM registration and data protection legislation. These initiatives helped lay the institutional foundations for Ghana’s expanding digital economy. His chairmanship of the International Telecommunication Union Council in 2009 further exposed him to international policy coordination and the complexities of global telecommunications governance. In an increasingly interconnected world, such experience has relevance beyond a single ministerial portfolio. Digital infrastructure, information governance and technological innovation now influence economic competitiveness, education, public administration and national security. His appointment as Minister for Trade and Industry between 2013 and 2014 introduced him to the challenges of industrial development, investment, enterprise competitiveness and the relationship between government policy and economic production. Although his tenure was comparatively brief, it broadened his understanding of the structural challenges confronting Ghana’s productive economy. He subsequently served as Minister for Employment and Labour Relations from 2014 to 2017. This portfolio required engagement with organised labour, employers, public institutions and other stakeholders whose interests do not always converge. Labour administration demands negotiation, patience, institutional understanding and the ability to balance competing economic and social priorities. These experiences are particularly relevant to Ghana’s development circumstances. The country’s economic transformation depends not only on expanding production but also on developing appropriate skills, improving labour productivity, strengthening industrial relations and creating sustainable employment opportunities. Haruna’s appointment as Minister for Education in January 2025 brought these experiences into another critical sector. Education is central to human capital development, national productivity, social mobility and the long-term competitiveness of the economy. It is also one of the most complex areas of public administration because its outcomes depend on the interaction of financing, infrastructure, personnel, curriculum, institutional governance and household circumstances. Together, these four ministerial portfolios reveal a significant pattern in Haruna’s political development. Communications concerns the infrastructure of a modern knowledge economy. Trade and Industry addresses production and economic competitiveness. Employment and Labour Relations addresses the relationship between economic activity, workers, and livelihoods. Education provides the human capabilities on which these sectors depend. This breadth of exposure offers a substantial foundation for understanding the interconnected nature of national development. However, experience must be distinguished from effectiveness. The ultimate value of these appointments depends on the policy outcomes achieved, the institutions strengthened and the improvements sustained beyond an individual’s tenure. Haruna’s parliamentary leadership adds another important dimension to this record. His appointment as Minority Leader following the NDC’s defeat in the 2016 general election placed him at the centre of national legislative politics during a period of intense political competition. Opposition leadership requires more than the ability to criticise government. It demands knowledge of parliamentary procedure, constitutional governance, public finance and legislative negotiation. It also requires the capacity to coordinate colleagues, articulate alternative policy positions and maintain working relationships across political divisions. During his tenure as Minority Leader, Haruna became one of Parliament’s most prominent voices, and his leadership led to the selection of a Speaker of Parliament who was then an opposition member. His contributions frequently demonstrated familiarity with legislative processes and the technical dimensions of national policy. His ability to engage complex issues, respond to political arguments and communicate institutional positions contributed to his visibility in Ghana’s political discourse. His replacement as Minority Leader in January 2023 represented a significant political setback. Yet leadership development is not defined exclusively by advancement. Political reversals can also test judgement, resilience, adaptability and commitment to institutional processes. The episode is noteworthy because it demonstrates the extent to which Haruna’s parliamentary experience had attracted recognition among colleagues. Equally important, his decision not to pursue the position illustrates the distinction between possessing political ambition and exercising judgement about when and how to pursue higher responsibility. These experiences are relevant to the national leadership question because Ghana’s political system requires individuals who understand both executive authority and legislative accountability. A president must work within constitutional constraints, engage Parliament, manage public institutions and negotiate competing national interests. Beyond formal appointments, his political personality has been shaped by communication, public engagement and an ability to operate across different political settings. Over the years, he has developed a recognisable communication style characterised by confidence, procedural knowledge and an ability to combine technical arguments with accessible political language. Effective political communication is not simply about eloquence. It involves explaining complex public decisions, establishing credibility, responding to criticism and building relationships across diverse constituencies. Haruna’s experience in student leadership, party organisation, Parliament and ministerial administration has provided repeated opportunities to develop these capabilities. His public presence often conveys confidence and familiarity with the issues under discussion. He has demonstrated an ability to engage technical audiences while communicating political positions in language accessible to the wider public. This combination contributes to the political aura and recognizability associated with his personality. Nevertheless, communication skills alone do not establish leadership competence. Charisma must be supported by sound judgement, administrative discipline, ethical conduct and measurable performance. The ability to persuade matters, but the capacity to implement policy, manage institutions, and account for results is even more consequential. Haruna, like every public figure, has strengths and weaknesses. His political decisions and leadership style have attracted both admiration and criticism. No political career spanning several decades can reasonably be expected to remain free of disagreement, controversy or difficult judgement calls. The appropriate measure of political maturity is therefore not personal perfection but the ability to learn from experience, respond constructively to criticism, and improve over time. His achievements should not exempt him from scrutiny, just as his shortcomings should not obscure the broader substance of his public service. Another important aspect of Haruna’s career is his engagement with younger generations. Having emerged through student and youth political structures, he has repeatedly acknowledged the importance of mentorship, leadership development, and creating opportunities for young people. He has publicly expressed a willingness to prepare younger individuals for political responsibility and has encouraged professional and alumni networks to support mentorship, internships, entrepreneurship and career development. These positions have wider national significance. Ghana’s development challenges include youth unemployment, limited access to economic opportunities and the need to prepare a new generation for leadership in public institutions, business and civil society. A sustainable leadership culture requires more than the continued prominence of established political figures. It depends on experienced leaders’ willingness to transfer knowledge, develop talent, and create pathways through which younger people can assume responsibility. Haruna’s involvement in sports development, including his association with football institutions such as Steadfast FC and Karela United, provides another dimension to his engagement with youth opportunity. Sports, like education and entrepreneurship, can provide platforms for talent development, social mobility and national participation. Although his political roots remain firmly associated with Northern Ghana, the significance of his career extends well beyond regional identity. His ministerial responsibilities, parliamentary leadership and participation in national policy debates have required engagement with institutions and stakeholders across the country. Any serious consideration of his political future must therefore be grounded in his national experience rather than regional affiliation. Ghana’s leadership challenges are national in character, even where their effects vary across communities. Prof. Eliasu Mumuni The writer is the Dean of the Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, University for Development Studies (UDS) Dean, Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, University for Development Studies (UDS)

items.title: FO rejects India's 'undiplomatic, irresponsible' remarks about Pakistan's mineral wealth
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday categorically rejected the “undiplomatic and irresponsible” remarks made by India at the United Nations regarding the country’s mineral wealth. At the UN Security Council (UNSC) Arria-formula meeting on natural resources and conflict, on Thursday India’s Permanent Representative to the UN Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish had “directly accused the Pakistan military of looting the country’s natural resources for personal gain and triggering domestic political turmoil to keep control over them”, according to Indian news agency ANI . The remarks had come after Pakistan raised the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) during the meeting, which has been held in abeyance by India following the attack in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26. In response to Harish’s remarks, Pakistan’s First Secretary Ansar Shah rejected the “frivolous and highly inappropriate remarks”. On Friday, the FO spokesperson was also asked about the Indian remarks during his weekly press briefing, to which he rejected the “undiplomatic and irresponsible” comments. “Such baseless accusations merit no attention and were immediately and effectively rebutted by Pakistan’s representative during the same meeting,” he said, adding that the remarks constituted “an unacceptable interference in Pakistan’s internal affairs” and were antithetical to the UN Charter. In a detailed statement released shortly after, the FO said: “Such diatribe, so typical of India, can only be rubbished.” “Instead of addressing Pakistan’s legitimate concerns with respect to India’s hydro-terrorism, India has resorted to unsubstantiated insinuations about Pakistan’s institutions and leadership,” the statement said. The statement highlighted that India’s hostility towards Pakistan’s development of its mineral resources was “equally evident in its persistent efforts to undermine Pakistan’s stability”. “Pakistan has repeatedly raised concerns, supported by evidence, regarding India’s sponsorship and support of terrorist activities in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, aimed at disrupting development and depriving local populations of the benefits of their natural resources,” the statement said. “India’s continuing descent into a Hindutva-inspired extremism-fascist polity, led by a religious fundamentalist regime is well known,” it added. “Indian accusations and distortion of facts are a futile attempt to hide its international isolation, and only aimed at distracting attention from India’s domestic situation and its weaponisation of shared resources, as evident from its illegal and unilateral action to hold the IWT in abeyance,” the statement said. The FO said that in August, the Court of Arbitration ruled that the treaty remains binding and fully in force and there was no legal basis for its unilateral suspension or termination. “India’s refusal to accept this ruling raises serious questions about its commitment to treaty obligations and international law,” it said. “Instead of misusing the platform of the UN for peddling lies, India will be well advised to implement its obligations under the UNSC resolutions on Jammu and Kashmir, where Indian occupation forces continue to perpetrate gross violations of human rights for decades,” it said. “A state that is a serial violator of UN Charter, UNSC resolutions, sovereignty of neighbouring states, and binding treaty obligations, that patronises systematic discrimination against its Muslim, Sikh, Christian, and Dalit minorities, engages in disinformation and terrorism as instruments of state policy and remains in forcible occupation of a territory whose people it denies the internationally guaranteed right to self-determination, has no standing whatsoever,” the FO remarked. “Instead of pointing fingers, India should introspect and change its behaviour,” it concluded.

items.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine’s allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
items.description: Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region. Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a “provocation” from Moscow. Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during one of its biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border. The cruise missile, designed for precision targets, crashed at about 06:30 (5:30GMT) and Natalie Szponar, a local resident, said she was getting her children ready for school when she heard a “whistle and a dull impact”. Another suspected missile went down near Rudnik nad Sanem to the west of Nowy Lipowiec, and a jet-powered drone crashed to the south near Mołodycz, said Kosiniak-Kamysz. He called the incursion into Polish airspace a “provocation” from Russia and said he would be asking Nato for additional support. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned “grave violations of Polish airspace” and said Nato jets had been scrambled in response. “This incident is clearly dangerous – a consequence of Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine,” he said. A UK- and France-led exercise called Koalicja 2026 is currently taking place in southeastern Poland involving 11 countries that are part of the West’s Coalition of the Willing group in preparation for a potential peace deal in Ukraine. “It is no coincidence that these objects landed near the site where military manoeuvres by a ‘coalition of the willing’ supported by Polish troops are taking place in Nowa Dęba,” Tusk told reporters on Friday. The violations of Polish airspace came a day after 40 countries took part in a Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, where the allies pledged continued support for Kyiv, and Chancellor Friedrich Merz said peace talks with Russia should take place soon on neutral territory. At least eight people were killed on Friday as Russian missiles and drones targeted three of Kyiv’s bridges across the River Dnipro and a station in Lviv, days after Russia’s Vladimir Putin threatened “painful” retaliation for repeated strikes on Russia’s bridge across the Kerch Strait to occupied Crimea. This is not the first time the war in Ukraine has spilled over into Poland and in July a cruise missile also landed in Poland.
