items.title: Bijoux, cuir et tissage : l’artisanat touareg au Musée national
items.description: © Internet La troisième Semaine internationale de l’artisanat touareg se poursuit jusqu’à dimanche. À Bamako, les pièces exposées racontent aussi le travail de celles et ceux qui les fabriquent. Bijoux, maroquinerie, tissages, sculptures et pierres naturelles occupent les espaces d’exposition du Musée national du Mali. Ouverte le 17 novembre, la rencontre organisée par l’association Timidwa s’achève le 22 novembre. Elle réunit artisans, acteurs culturels et visiteurs autour de savoir-faire transmis et renouvelés dans les ateliers. Le thème de cette édition associe le patrimoine touareg à l’éducation, à la culture et à l’intégration des pays de l’AES. À l’ouverture, le ministre Mossa Ag Attaher représentait son collègue chargé de l’Artisanat et de la Culture, Mamou Daffé. Les interventions officielles ont insisté sur la transmission des techniques et sur l’activité économique que représente l’artisanat. Pour les exposants, quelques jours au Musée national offrent surtout la possibilité de montrer leurs pièces et de rencontrer directement le public. Anas Ag Mohamed Lamine, membre de Timidwa et artisan présent au salon, a rappelé dans un entretien publié le 19 novembre que ce travail fait vivre ses praticiens. Cette parole ramène la manifestation à une réalité simple : derrière un objet présenté comme patrimoine, il y a aussi un métier et la recherche de clients. La semaine mêle exposition et prestations musicales. Son intérêt se joue dans ces échanges entre artisans et visiteurs, au-delà des discours de la cérémonie d’ouverture. Les ventes et les contacts noués pendant la manifestation seront connus des participants après sa clôture.

items.title: Sans Édouard Philippe, Gabriel Attal en tête d’une primaire de la droite et du centre
items.description: Un sondage Ifop publie le 18 novembre place Gabriel Attal en position de force dans l'hypothese d'une primaire du centre sans edouard Philippe . L'ancien Premier ministre recueillerait 38 % des intentions de vote, devant David Lisnard (33 %) et Bruno Retailleau (29 %). Avec le candidat d'Horizons, le match serait beaucoup plus serre. Un scrutin en preparation malgre les resistances Les equipes de Gabriel Attal (Renaissance), Bruno Retailleau (Les Republicains) et David Lisnard (Nouvelle energie) ont pose les premiers jalons d'une primaire ouverte, pressentie pour fin janvier (17-24 ou 24-31). Une cotisation faible, autour de deux euros, est evoquee pour elargir la participation. Environ 38 % des electeurs envisagent d'y prendre part. edouard Philippe refuse toujours de s'y joindre . « Je n'y participerai pas, point », a-t-il repete. Sur X, son porte-parole Jeremie Patrier-Leitus a reagi au contexte des sondages : « edouard Philippe est le seul candidat de la droite et du centre qui peut acceder au 2nd tour… Cessons ces discussions interminables sur cette primaire qui n'a aucun sens ». ❗️Le dernier sondage Ifop-Fiducial pour Sud Radio est sans appel! 🇫🇷@EPhilippe_LH est le seul candidat de la droite et du centre qui peut accéder au 2nd tour de l’élection présidentielle! ❌Ni David Lisnard, ni Bruno Retailleau, ni Gabriel Attal ne sont en mesure d’empêcher un duel mortifère entre Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon. ❗️Cessons ces discussions interminables sur cette primaire qui n’a aucun sens qui créera de la division et de la confusion et construisons urgemment le rassemblement de la droite et du centre! @Avec_Edouard @JeunesEdouard — Jérémie Patrier-Leitus (@JPatrierLeitus) November 20, 2026 Gabriel Attal a reconnu le 19 novembre sur France 2 qu'il n'avait « pas convaincu » les Francais « a ce stade ». Il assume pourtant le risque de la primaire : « Peut-etre qu'a la fin ce ne sera pas moi ». Il a aussi affirme que « si edouard Philippe voulait participer a cette primaire, elle aurait deja eu lieu », tout en plaidant pour sa presence. 🔴 “Peut-être qu’à la fin ce ne sera pas moi, si la primaire a lieu et que je ne la gagne pas”. Gabriel Attal assume la “prise de risque” si une primaire de la droite et du centre est organisée. #HeuredeVérité https://t.co/oP0KZPahIs — L'Heure de Vérité (@hdeverite_ftv) November 19, 2026 Dans le scenario a quatre, David Lisnard prendrait un leger avantage (29 %), suivi d'edouard Philippe (28 %), Gabriel Attal (25 %) et Bruno Retailleau (18 %). Frederic Dabi (Ifop) note que Gabriel Attal beneficie d'une bonne image a droite grâce a son discours sur l'ordre et la fermete. Les sympathisants d'Horizons se reporteraient d'abord vers Lisnard (48 %) en cas d'absence de leur champion. L'objectif affiche reste d'eviter un second tour entre Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Melenchon. Une nouvelle reunion des equipes Attal-Retailleau-Lisnard est prevue la semaine du 23 novembre pour trancher les modalites restantes, notamment la charte des valeurs et le perimetre. David Lisnard souhaite une competition « la plus large possible », tandis que Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau s'opposent a l'inclusion d'eric Zemmour.

items.description: La filiale du groupe algerien Sonelgaz (Sonelgaz International) et la societe ivoirienne CI-energies ont signe trois contrats strategiques le 18 novembre a Abidjan, en marge de la deuxieme edition du Salon international des ressources extractives et de l'energie et en presence du ministre algerien de l'energie et des energies renouvelables, Mourad Adjal, et de son homologue ivoirien, Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly. Une convention-cadre a ete conclue, portant sur les contours de la cooperation et le partenariat entre les deux entreprises. Deux autres contrats ont egalement ete signes pour le developpement des capacites de production electrique et des infrastructures de distribution d'electricite, rapporte l'agence de presse algerienne APS. Un communique de Sonelgaz a indique que la signature des contrats marque une evolution de la cooperation entre les deux societes, passant de la coordination et de l'echange d'expertises a la phase de concretisation sur le terrain des projets, en mettant a profit les capacites techniques et d'ingenierie ainsi que le savoir-faire accumule par les entreprises algeriennes dans les differentes filieres de l'industrie electrique. Construction d'une centrale electrique de 40 megawatts L'un des contrats porte sur le renforcement de la production electrique ivoirienne grâce a un projet de construction d'une centrale electrique d'une capacite de 40 megawatts (MW), par l'installation de deux turbines de 20 MW chacune fonctionnant au combustible liquide ou au gaz naturel. L'electricite produite devrait ensuite etre acheminee vers le poste 225 kV de San Pedro 2, dont la construction est en cours, indique la presse algerienne. Pour sa part, le ministre algerien de l'energie et des energies renouvelables, Mourad Adjal, a annonce que le calendrier previsionnel prevoit l'execution du projet au premier trimestre 2027. Un contrat pour developper les reseaux de distribution et ameliorer les infrastructures electriques La cooperation algero-ivoirienne se concretise aussi par un contrat pour fournir des installations et des equipements electriques visant a ameliorer le reseau de distribution en Cote d'Ivoire, notamment des postes mobiles, des transformateurs et autres equipements de haute et moyenne tension. Sonelgaz apportera en outre des camions-laboratoires et une assistance technique pour localiser les defauts et pour la maintenance des câbles souterrains, qui seront operationnels a Abidjan et dans d'autres villes du pays. La societe algerienne Sonelgaz International affiche resolument l'orientation de sa societe mere vers les marches africains, en apportant son expertise aux partenaires continentaux dans le secteur de la production electrique et de la fourniture de gaz naturel.

items.title: Short-term inflation reaches 10.41pc on costly flour
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 19, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday. The index, comprising 51 items, whose prices are collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services. The data showed that the prices of 23 commodities increased, while those of eight items declined. Meanwhile, the prices of 20 items remained unchanged from the previous week. Short-term inflation has remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely due to persistently elevated petrol and diesel prices. However, oil prices have been slowly declining for the past few days. During the 21 days leading up to Nov 20, petrol prices fell from Rs396.06 to Rs322 per litre , while diesel prices declined from Rs398.80 to Rs355 per litre . This represented reductions of about Rs74 and Rs43.80 per litre, respectively. The impact of this decline was visible in the week-on-week review. The SPI declined by 0.65pc week-on-week, reflecting a declining oil prices. This is the second consecutive week that SPI recorded a marginal decline on a WoW basis. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has expressed concern over rising transport fares across the country and directed provincial governments to take urgent measures to reduce passenger and freight fares in line with the decline in petrol and diesel prices. Chairing an emergency meeting of the National Price Monitoring Committee (NPMC) on Thursday, the minister asked the provinces to issue revised fare notifications through the relevant departments and ensure strict compliance. Meanwhile, the items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included eggs (8.84pc), potatoes (8.07pc), wheat flour (4.42pc), chicken (3.01pc), bananas (1.74pc), georgette (1.40pc), shirting (0.76pc), garlic (0.62pc), vegetable ghee 2.5kg (0.54pc), cooked beef (0.46pc) and firewood (0.34pc). Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (30.55pc), onions (9.17pc), LPG (6.46pc), petrol (3.87pc), diesel (2.46pc), pulse moong (0.54pc), gur (0.08pc) and sugar (0.07pc). On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included LPG (87.99pc), wheat flour (44.20pc), electricity for Q1 (36.30pc), diesel (24.84pc), chicken (24.35pc), onions (24.05pc), petrol (21.35pc), chilies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.60pc), bread plain (12.35pc), beef (11.10pc) and milk fresh (8.96pc). In contrast, potatoes prices fell by 27.13pc, sugar (26.24pc), tomatoes (20.86pc), eggs (16.10pc), salt powder (11.03pc), pulse masoor (6.90pc), gur (6.52pc) and pulse moong (5.81pc). Last week , short-term inflation rose to 11.21pc year-on-year driven largely by perishable food products.

items.title: Carburant à Kayes : l’essence plus disponible, les prix surveillés
items.description: © Dirpa Les réserves annoncées par les services du commerce ont fortement augmenté. Un autre convoi de citernes est arrivé dans la ville jeudi. La Direction régionale du commerce a présenté, le 19 novembre, un stock d’essence de 1 993 952 litres pour la région de Kayes, contre 856 700 litres lors du précédent relevé. Le gasoil est passé de 896 125 à 904 849 litres. Ces chiffres ont été communiqués pendant une réunion du comité régional chargé du suivi de la situation des hydrocarbures. Pour les conducteurs, les transporteurs et les commerces tributaires des livraisons, la disponibilité à la pompe compte autant que le volume entreposé. Le directeur régional du commerce, Robo Bayo, estime que les stocks des stations couvrent les besoins en essence et en gasoil. Il indique également que les prix restent globalement stables dans la région. Cette surveillance a déjà eu des suites. Deux opérateurs ont été sanctionnés après des signalements portant sur le non-respect des prix réglementés. L’approvisionnement et le prix payé par le client figurent ainsi dans le même suivi régional. Un nouveau convoi de camions-citernes est arrivé à Kayes le 19 novembre, sous escorte des Forces armées maliennes. Le volume transporté n’a pas été précisé dans l’annonce de la Direction régionale du commerce. Les chiffres présentés au comité et cette arrivée donnent une image plus favorable des réserves d’essence, tandis que la régularité des livraisons restera déterminante pour les stations et les usagers.

items.title: Ghana Association of Banks and GhIPSS rally public behind GhanaPay as nation accelerates toward a cashless economy
items.description: The Ghana Association of Banks (GAB), in partnership with the Ghana Interbank Payment and Settlement Systems Limited (GhIPSS), has intensified its nationwide awareness drive for GhanaPay, positioning the bank-backed mobile money service as the cornerstone of Ghana’s transition toward a modern, cash-lite economy. Speaking during a high-level media engagement in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, industry leaders underscored why the widespread adoption of GhanaPay is especially opportune. As global commerce and everyday transactions undergo rapid digitisation, consumers and businesses require payment infrastructure that is not only fast and convenient, but also deeply integrated into the formal financial system. “The world is moving away from just financial inclusion,” noted John Awuah, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Banks. “Ghana has made significant strides, moving from about 41 percent financial inclusion a decade ago to over 80 percent today. Now, we are talking about financial health—ensuring that once people are included, there are no cost barriers or hindrances blocking them from free access to financial services. That is where GhanaPay delivers.” Backed by Every Bank Across Ghana Unlike conventional telecommunications-led mobile wallets, GhanaPay is an industry-wide mobile money service owned and backed by the entire Ghanaian banking sector. It is directly accessible through all universal banks, savings and loans companies, and rural and community banks nationwide. Whether a user resides in a major commercial hub or a rural community, their wallet is anchored by a regulated financial institution of their choice. Unmatched Advantages Over Conventional Alternatives During the engagement, stakeholders highlighted several structural advantages that set GhanaPay apart in Ghana’s digital payments landscape: Zero Transfer Fees: Users pay zero transaction charges on transfers, removing the cost friction that often discourages frequent digital payments and directly supporting everyday financial health. 5% Interest on Wallet Balances: Money held in a GhanaPay wallet works for the user, attracting upto a 5% interest rate—turning everyday spending balances into productive savings. A Direct Pathway to Credit for the Banked and Unbanked: Users do not need an existing bank account to register for GhanaPay. However, because every wallet is linked to an affiliate bank, consistent transactions build a verifiable digital money trail. For both banked and previously unbanked individuals, small traders, and entrepreneurs, this empirical financial footprint makes it significantly easier to qualify for bank loans and credit facilities at competitive rates. Multifunctional Financial Ecosystem: Beyond standard money transfers, bill payments, and airtime top-ups, GhanaPay is built with specialized value-added tools: Sponsored Wallets: Allows parents, guardians, employers, or sponsors to allocate funds to dependents or staff with controlled spending limits. Crowdfunding (Susu): Enables alumni associations, community groups, churches, and social clubs to transparently pool funds and track contributions. Platform Agnostic & Universal Access: GhanaPay works seamlessly across all mobile networks using a customer’s existing phone number. Smartphone users can access the full suite of features via the mobile app, while feature-phone users can transact effortlessly via USSD by dialing *707# —and can even be set up with an app-linked wallet. Multi-Layered Security: Built on GhIPSS’s ISO 27001 and PCI-DSS certified banking infrastructure, GhanaPay protects users with double—and even triple—layers of security, combining PIN protection, One-Time Password (OTP) two-factor authentication, biometric fingerprint verification, and strict Ghana Card identity validation. Nationwide Redemption at ATMs and Banks: Funds and payment tokens on GhanaPay can be cashed in or redeemed seamlessly across bank branches, ATMs, and designated GhanaPay agents nationwide. Clemencia Tetteh, Head of Corporate Affairs and Communications at GhIPSS, reaffirmed the institutions’ commitment to continuous innovation: “We recognize that we must continuously listen, innovate, and improve. Our commitment is to ensure that GhanaPay remains responsive to the evolving digital financial needs of customers and contributes meaningfully to Ghana’s financial inclusion and digital transformation agenda.” How to Get Started and Connect Ghanaians can download the GhanaPay Customer app today on the Google Play Store (for Android devices) or the Apple App Store (for iOS devices), dial *707# on any mobile network, or visit any participating bank branch or designated agent with a valid Ghana Card to register. For further information, onboarding support, and campaign updates, the public is encouraged to visit the official platforms or reach out via the toll-free helpline: Official GhanaPay Website: www.ghanapay.com.gh Ghana Association of Banks (GAB): www.gab.com.gh GhIPSS Portal & FAQs: www.ghipss.net Social Media: Follow GhanaPay (@GhanaPay / GhanaPayMobileMoney) on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Toll-Free Customer Support: 0800-000-707 For media inquiries, interviews, and syndication requests, contact the Ghana Association of Banks (GAB) via info@gab.com.gh or 0302-667138 / 0302-670629.

items.title: The Old-School Dating Ritual People Can’t Seem to Shake
items.description: A man and woman leave a restaurant. “I had a nice time—” she begins, but he’s already off, skateboarding away with nothing more than a “Call me.” Then she receives a Venmo request: “your half.” Out pops the actor Julia Fox, here to impart a warning. She shows a montage of how a relationship might unfold with this scruffy, nonchalant man—flashes of him playing video games in a filthy apartment, holding an umbrella over himself while she gets drenched, presenting her with a cheap engagement ring. The message is clear: If he won’t pay for your dinner now, he’ll be a stingy, unchivalrous man-child forever. This trailer isn’t for Fox’s next film. It’s for the new “Anti 50/50 Campaign” she’s promoting with the dating site Seeking, which involves a $50,000 fund to reimburse singles who have split the check on a date (up to $50 a person). “Seeking is challenging what it sees as a decline in generosity,” the press release reads. That statement is not gender-neutral. In the company’s own survey, 75 percent of women said they prefer men to “take the lead on dates,” including planning and paying—yet 61 percent of female Zoomers said they’ve been asked to share the bill. Seeking regards this as an affront to straight women everywhere. “I’m all for women being independent,” Fox says in the release, “but that doesn’t mean we have to entertain low-effort men who think splitting a check is the height of romance. If you’re going to court somebody, COURT THEM.” Of all the causes Fox could take up in our year 2026, this one is oddly old-fashioned. But Seeking is taking advantage of something real: The expectation that men should foot the bill, especially on the first date, is still stubbornly ubiquitous , even among women who see themselves as progressive or critical of strict gender norms. In a dating world that can feel hard and confusing, many singles are looking for explicit rules—and many straight women are looking for a man who offers care and consistency. Alas, a paid check does not a gentleman make. [ Read: Bumble moves the first move back to men ] The bill-paying convention, like it or not, has its roots in a philosophy of clear-cut gender difference: Men are born providers and leaders, whereas women are passive and dependent. For many years, this was the logic by which American society generally operated. Women had precious few career opportunities; their presumed job was to be a wife and mother. So in the early 20th century, when more women began dating in public spaces rather than having suitors visit their home, men were expected to pay . They were the ones with money to fork up. Now, though, a far greater number of women are financially self-sufficient. In this context, the assumption that men should pay for dates seems a bit weird, and weirdly pervasive. For her 2020 book, The Mating Game: How Gender Still Shapes How We Date , the Appalachian State University sociologist Ellen Lamont interviewed college-educated young adults and found that more than two-thirds of women participants said that all of their first dates were covered by the man. Many of them would offer to split the check as a test, hoping that the man would insist on paying. One 27-year-old told Lamont that she didn’t find it important for a man to grab the first check, but “I would expect it, and then if he expected me to pay for half, or if he expected me to pay, then I’d be like, I’m out .” So it was important, then? Lamont clarified. “I guess it is,” the woman conceded. “’Cause I’d be like, man, he didn’t even pay, what a douche.” Lamont has found that courtship norms are unusually sticky. Many people dismiss the idea of stark, inherent gender differences in other realms—they think that women are just as equipped as men to have a career, or that men should be equally involved parents. Yet at the same time, they quietly maintain that men should be the ones to ask women out, pay for dates, suggest exclusivity or commitment, and propose marriage. People are motivated by their own interests, after all; women fought for the right to vote and to enter the workforce not just for the abstract concept of equality but also because they wanted a say and a paycheck. A woman might find splitting the bill about as appealing as a man might view splitting the housework. And guidelines can be comforting, especially for a ritual as intimidating as dating. No one wants to misstep. So people tend to follow the rules—even rules they don’t fully stand behind in theory. They rationalize, of course. Some people have told me that men should get the tab because they make more money on average. (If this was really the logic, shouldn’t the higher-earning person pay, whoever it may be?) Others—including some men I’ve spoken with—hold that the least men can do is front the bill, given that the woman otherwise tends to bring more to the table: better listening skills, empathy, social graces. The man, according to this line of thinking, is lucky to be there at all, whereas the woman has more to lose—especially in a climate of misogyny and prevalent harassment. But putting women on such a pedestal, presuming that they’re inherently soft and nurturing and pulled together, is flattening in its own way. Many women also see willingness to pay as a sign of genuine interest: “an easy gimme,” Lamont said, particularly for young women who have recently left college hookup culture behind and are looking for courtship that feels serious and grown-up. Regardless of gender, reading someone’s feelings is difficult. And a lot of women look for tokens of dedication, she said, because they’ve been told again and again that men are commitment-phobic libertines. Something as prosaic as a credit card in a cup, when you’re scanning for green flags, can take on outsize significance. This was true at the time of Lamont’s research, and it may be even truer now, when a lot of straight women are fed up with a perceived lack of enthusiasm from male prospects. The dating app Bumble, once known for its “women message first” policy, now allows men to initiate; when the company surveyed women, it found that many were tired of putting themselves out there and wanted men to step up—to be present, active, eager. Meanwhile, a slew of think pieces have captured a similar yearning. “Lately I have been bruised by the ambivalence of men,” the writer Jean Garnett wrote in The New York Times , recalling a man who’d canceled their date when he was feeling anxious. “Where were the men who could handle hard stuff? Like leaving the house for sex?” The headline of another Times story summed up the sentiment: “Men, Where Have You Gone? Please Come Back.” The problem is that bill paying alone isn’t actually a good gauge of emotional investment. Many of the men Lamont interviewed told her that they’d grab the check even when they had no interest in seeing their date again. A man can also be rich, keen, and a self-involved jerk. (A 2016 study of university students in California found that, among male participants, embracing traditional courtship norms was associated with “hostile sexism” and the disavowal of feminism.) On the flip side, a man who suggests splitting the bill might be earnestly trying to foster an equitable dynamic. Or maybe he just doesn’t have the money to throw down $100 every time he takes someone out, and maybe—going out on a limb here—being broke doesn’t make someone a lazy schlub. A ton of single people today, men and women alike, say they’re forgoing dating because it’s too expensive . The team behind Seeking understands this on some level; the company refers to “rising dating costs and growing frustration with the modern dating experience” as its raison d’être—but it seems to find that strain to be a problem for only half the population. When men see dating as cost-prohibitive, though, that’s an issue for straight women too. Where have the men gone? Perhaps home to spare their aching wallet. [ Read: The dystopia of modern singlehood ] If courtship is going to evolve beyond outdated gender expectations, the transition will not always feel smooth. Women who want new models of masculinity will need to let go of old ones—trading the comfort of paternalism for the satisfaction of being seen as a capable adult, or the convenience of covered costs for a connection between equals. And sometimes, two people will have to chuckle at the awkwardness of not knowing who initiates or pays or plans. I actually find this to be a sweet part of dating: when both people reach for their card, lock eyes, and laugh; or when one gets to show that they’re having fun by saying, “I’ll get us next time.” Eventually, you realize that, despite plenty of ambiguity, you’ve both been trading little affirmations back and forth, one person texting first, the other suggesting a location or giving a compliment. You find that uncertainty can be survived. And only by working through it together do you discover what fits—not for men and women as abstract categories, but for two distinct human beings. ​​When you buy a book using a link on this page, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic.

items.title: My Week as a Kardashian
items.description: L ooking back , I’m not sure why I’d expected subtlety from a garment whose name promised to defy physics—especially one that I’d ordered from Kim Kardashian’s shapewear-and-loungewear company, Skims. But when I first tried the “Butt Lifting Short” under the dress I planned to wear to my father’s 80th birthday party, then asked my mother for a second opinion, her eyes widened. “Well, they’re a little bit of a statement,” she said—the same phrase, in the same tone, that she had used when, as a teenager, I had asked her what she thought about nose rings. This was my first mistake with a Kardashian-branded item, but it would not be my last. I’d wanted to understand just how much America’s most famous influencers had infiltrated American consumption. So for seven days in October, while on a trip to visit my parents in the center of the Kardashians’ universe (Los Angeles), everything I put on and in my body came from companies associated with the Kardashian daughters; their mother, Kris; and their half sisters, Kendall and Kylie Jenner. The family’s dedication to launching brand after brand, in product category after product category, had made it easy to obtain everything I needed to live a life made in their image: Clothes. Food. Drinks. Cosmetics. Supplements. Cleaning supplies. Novelty socks. My usual aesthetic oscillates between office casual and babysitting casual, so I didn’t expect to covet much from brands whose standout products include lipstick that tries to mimic the look of lip filler and a slip dress that makes everybody look positively bodacious. When I drove to the Skims store to swap my shapewear for something less shapely, I had every intention of making my exchange and leaving. But then I saw the cashmere sweatpants. And the silky pajamas. And the leggings—a genre of clothing plucked from the depths of hell to make women insecure about their thighs—which somehow looked nice on the women modeling for their friends outside the dressing rooms. One reason I’d never bought into the Kardashians’ world was that I had no interest in looking like Jessica Rabbit. But I was interested in these delicious cashmere sweatpants. Hours into accepting the Kardashians into my life, did I already want what they were selling? These days, the Kardashians are somewhat less visible than they were in the 2000s and 2010s, when Keeping Up With the Kardashians was still airing on E! , and millions of Americans knew by osmosis that Kourtney was on-again, off-again with Scott and that Kylie had finally admitted to using lip filler. Their current reality show— The Kardashians , on Hulu—is less beloved by fans than their original show , and although Kim has 343 million followers on Instagram, she has gone from being the most-followed person on the platform, circa 2014, to the eighth. (According to one account that tracks such metrics, Kylie is neck and neck with the Rock for the No. 5 spot.) “But it doesn’t matter anymore,” MJ Corey, the author of Dekonstructing the Kardashians , told me. Even if the Kardashians are themselves less omnipresent, because of their many product lines, they’re more ubiquitous than ever. For my week living in the Kardashian brandiverse, I wore clothes from Skims and Khloé’s Good American brand; did my makeup with Kylie Cosmetics’ Kyliner, Kylash, and Kybrow; and even pulled my hair back with hair ties from Skims’s collaboration with the mulberry-silk company Slip. I swapped my morning coffee for Kim’s energy drinks, sprinkled Kylie’s K 2 O “skin hydration mix” into my water, snacked on Khloé’s Khloud protein popcorn, and ate meals from the L.A. fast-casual restaurant chain Health Nut, which Kris has invested in. At night, I washed my face with 111Skin products—another investment—only because Kim’s skin-care line won’t launch until next year. I thought oral care was the last product vertical that the Kardashians hadn’t touched, so I used Crest—only to learn later that I could have been using purple color-correcting toothpaste from Moon, an oral-care company that Kendall has invested in. In an attempt to reach a moment of peak Kardashian-ness (at least as I imagined it), I drove to Health Nut later that week in the bodacious Skims dress. Before I left the car, I applied my Kylie Cosmetics lip kit duo of lip liner and lipstick; its patented HotFlux technology temporarily plumped my lips by essentially burning them, but I told myself that a true Kardashian would know that beauty is pain. (Kim once wore a corset so tight, she described breathing in it as an “art form.”) By the time I’d ordered my salad—a romaine, mozzarella, and sprout concoction straight out of 2007—I looked, for better or worse, like I’d gotten some Juvéderm lip filler. When I returned home, I donned a complimentary face mask included in my 111Skin order, because in the Kardashian world, one can never have too much skin care. In my bedazzled Skims claw clip, Kylie lip products, Good American T-shirt, and Skims hoodie and yoga pants, I felt precisely how the slogan on my Rob Kardashian novelty socks described me: a “Classy Bitch.” Kathy Bidart Walecki F rom the beginning of Keeping Up With the Kardashians , the family has been working the same hustle: They sell a view into their world, and then use that screen time to advertise their products. Even in Season 1, the sisters’ boutique, Dash, served as a key setting and occasional plot driver. As the show scaled, so did Dash: A spin-off series, Kourtney and Khloé Take Miami , revolved around the sisters opening a new location, and the spin-off to the spin-off, Kim and Kourtney Take New York , was about opening one in SoHo. Dash became a fan pilgrimage site; it was also one of the Kardashian ventures criticized for being insultingly expensive. Similarly, SKKN by Kim shut down after getting ridiculed for its $600 skin-care routine; the Kardashian Kard, a prepaid debit card that cost $99.95 to activate for a year, was scrapped the same month it launched. The family also developed a bit of a snake-oil-salesman reputation for making sponsored Instagram posts about QuickTrim weight-loss supplements (basically caffeine pills) and Flat Tummy teas (basically laxatives). But over the years, the family has found more reputable products to sell at a lower price point—often with the help of business leaders such as Emma Grede, who has worked with them on several of their most successful brands. The daughters have concentrated on launching companies that represent their archetypes: Kim, the curvy one, has shapewear; Kendall, the enigmatic tomboy, has 818 Tequila; Kylie, famous for her voluptuous lips and meticulous makeup, has Kylie Cosmetics; Khloé, who was subjected to ceaseless comments about her weight, launched a size-inclusive clothing company. And Kourtney, who is so health-conscious that she once objected to candy being served at her child’s Candyland-themed birthday party, has a supplement line, Lemme. (Kourtney declined to be interviewed for this story; the rest of the Kardashian-Jenners did not respond to interview requests.) Some of these brands have been extraordinarily successful. Another beauty company bought 51 percent of Kylie Cosmetics for $600 million in 2019; Skims is worth $5 billion (four times as much as Spanx, which essentially invented modern shapewear). The day that Skims announced a collaboration with Nike, the athletic brand’s market value went up by $6.7 billion . Kim became a billionaire in 2021, and the entire family, at least according to some estimates, has amassed a net worth roughly equivalent to the GDP of Belize. Which is to say, the Kardashians have long since become so wealthy that the people they’re selling products to have zero chance of keeping up with their lifestyles (if that was ever possible). What they’re selling instead is a splurge for the middle-ish class. To anyone who shops at J.Crew or Madewell, Good American prices would feel comparable; Skims products generally sell for about the same as Spanx’s. Many Kardashian brands are carried at Walmart, Target, and Ulta, a Sephora competitor with a slightly lower price point. A full Kardashian transformation wasn’t cheap: It cost me about $3,000, enough that my credit-card company sent me fraud alerts twice because its algorithms could not comprehend why I—a person who doesn’t spend much on clothing or cosmetics—had suddenly dropped so much on Skims and skin care. But for many Americans, buying just a bit of the family’s world is within reach. Because of their early days hawking Flat Tummy teas online, I hadn’t expected much from the Kardashians’ products, but some of them were indeed superior to my norm. As someone who doesn’t take a multivitamin and just hopes for the best, I looked forward to taking my citrus-flavored immunity gummies from Lemme, every morning. Several people complimented my Good American jeans, and the Kylie Cosmetics’ products really were long-lasting—plus, for those wanting to look like they’d gotten Juvéderm, the lip kit is a cheaper alternative. I wouldn’t say shapewear by any brand is actually comfortable, but Skims did make being encased, sausage-like, in nylon relatively painless. But that was the good stuff. My order from Kris’s cleaning company, Safely, never arrived, so I gave up and used Dawn. I did not expect Kylie’s K 2 O drink mix to actually “increase skin elasticity & reduce wrinkles & fine lines,” as the package claimed, but I did expect it to be drinkable. I never figured out how to get the powder to fully dissolve, so I periodically swallowed peach-flavored clumps of trademarked “bioactive collagen peptides.” Consuming Khloud’s white-cheddar protein popcorn was worse: Imagine chewing Styrofoam coated in pulverized drywall. (A couple of my friends have told me that the kettle-corn variety isn’t as bad.) At least I had Khloud Plus protein chips, also featuring collagen. The nacho flavor was good enough, in a nacho-flavored-tree-bark sort of way. Anyone who wanted to go to a restaurant with me knew that the meal would need to be at Health Nut. I made the 30-minute drive there a few times a week to stock up on salads, sandwiches, and a delightful iced green-tea drink known as the Mango Greentini. I became the restaurant’s most devoted regular, except perhaps for the Kardashian-Jenners, who regularly consumed the salads on Keeping Up With the Kardashians . But it did not save me from the times when I had to watch my parents drink coffee while I sipped Kim’s Update energy drinks. Desperate for a warm morning beverage, I tried heating the drinks up, but that didn’t help much: They still tasted of Pez and contained a caffeine alternative that gave me the urge to clench my jaw. I couldn’t tell if my loss of appetite meant that my Lemme supplements, which supposedly “promote your body’s GLP-1 production,” were actually working, or that I simply dreaded the Khloud popcorn. But soon enough, I settled into my Kardashian routine. My parents started alerting our loved ones to my project before family gatherings, to ward off any concerns that I’d suddenly developed a penchant for dressing like a Mafia wife on her way to Pilates. The distance between my life and that of some of the most successful influencers of our era seemed slightly smaller, because now I was someone who relaxed in dedicated loungewear and not just a sweatshirt from her high-school softball team. Like the Kardashians, I now went out in public dressed, for work, in clothes so tight that they might as well have been body paint—and, yes, those clothes did get me more stares than I was used to. And while I was driving back and forth to Health Nut on canyon roads overlooking the Pacific Ocean, I was reminded that—like Kim—I might rent in New York City, but California was my forever home . In fact, my parents’ house is close enough to the Kardashians’ in Calabasas that when a wildfire caused a power outage during my visit, both areas were affected, according to an outage map. Do they have a full-house generator? I wondered, as I sat in the dark in my Kylie lip liner. Kathy Bidart Walecki B y the end of day seven , when I took a shot of Kendall’s 818 Tequila to celebrate my release from the Kardashians’ grip, it didn’t feel like much of a finale. The Kardashian brand ecosystem had been easy enough to inhabit. The bodacious Skims dress—which, like the Butt Lifting Short, proved too powerful for its own good—had mostly stayed in my closet. (My mom had also forbidden me from wearing it to church.) Good American’s more casual offerings had meant that I could wear jeans and T-shirts as usual, and the family’s skin-care products, cosmetics, and salads had fit fairly seamlessly into my routine. I had even started to sort of like the Khloud popcorn—although maybe that was just Stockholm syndrome, which science tells us can set in after six days. In the weeks since that tequila shot, I’ve still used Kardashian products and have frequently found myself forgetting that they’re Kardashian products at all. Some of their brands, such as Khloud, still trade on the family members’ fame by featuring them in ads and on packaging, but many of them don’t. I’d expected the Los Angeles Skims store to be a shrine to Kim, but I didn’t see an image of her anywhere. The store’s minimalist, curvaceous design was meant to highlight beige shapewear and beige shapewear only. In a way, that’s a testament to Skims’s success: Over the past five years, Google searches for the brand have occasionally outnumbered searches for Kim herself. Maybe the family is quietly coming to accept that they are no longer the cultural centerpiece that they were in the 2010s. The Kardashians have spent two decades vying for people’s attention, and now they have to fight a new generation of YouTube and TikTok creators. But if there is any logical end point to influencing, it may be in the same playbook that Chip and Joanna Gaines have used to build their home-goods juggernaut and that Gwyneth Paltrow has used for Goop: merchandise. By that measure, the Kardashian product empire is the best outcome that any influencer could aspire to. The family has monetized their fame to the point that people still buy their products even if those customers are no longer paying as much attention to them. Instagram likes are fleeting, but Khloud popcorn could probably survive a nuclear blast. The Kardashians do seem to be giving viewers less of themselves than they used to. Keeping Up With the Kardashians went off the air in 2021, and even the title of their Hulu show, The Kardashians , seems to acknowledge that viewers can’t really keep up with them anymore. Fans tend to complain that the new series is boring. The eighth season, currently airing, is basically product placement for the girls’ businesses: Kim debuts NikeSKIMS; Kendall does an event for 818 Tequila; Khloé feels awkward during a steamy photoshoot with a male model for her new perfume line, XO Blue by Khloé Kardashian. (While shooting, she and the model, Brandon, discuss how the line is going to be available at Sephora.) Hulu did not reply when I asked for viewership numbers, but I can’t imagine that a show in which a major plotline involves Kourtney’s stepson getting his driver’s license gets as many eyeballs as Season 8 of Keeping Up With the Kardashians . Yes, that one included a photoshoot for their brother’s sock company, but it was mostly about Kim having a baby with the rapper Kanye West (now known as Ye). The Kardashians’ shows were always a business endeavor, but more and more, part of what they’re selling is the ability to watch them sell us things. For now, the Kardashians are still grinding. They have a show and several spin-offs; they post pictures and videos of themselves on social media. They still trade on the idea that their lives are glamorous enough—or at least strange enough—that we should both pay attention to them and purchase bits of their lifestyles. If more of the sisters’ products reach Skims-level heights, they may no longer need to spend half their time advertising their merchandise. But would they really want that? Kim has presented herself for years as a businesswoman first and foremost: Her recently released authorized biography, Citizen Kim , includes a family history of the several generations of mother-daughter duos w ho started antique shops, beauty parlors, and children’s-clothing boutiques and grew them into local retail dynasties. The Kardashians love attention, yes, but they really love to sell—their image, their drama, their products. Some of those products, it turns out, are pretty good. I wouldn’t recommend that you build your life around them, and I definitely wouldn’t recommend K 2 O. But after a week inside the family’s brandiverse, I am surprised to feel more impressed than terrified when I consider that America may never escape the Kardashians.

items.title: Kinguélé Aval : le raccordement achevé, 35 MW attendus sur le réseau électrique en décembre
items.description: Le raccordement du poste électrique de la centrale hydroélectrique de Kinguélé Aval à la ligne haute tension de 225 kV est effectif. Après les travaux d'interconnexion, les équipes techniques sont engagées dans les essais d'ensemble avant l'injection annoncée de 35 MW supplémentaires sur le réseau national dans quelques semaines. Vue aérienne du barrage de Kinguéle Aval. © D.R. Le projet hydroélectrique de Kinguélé Aval approche de son entrée en exploitation. Les travaux de raccordement de son poste électrique à la ligne de transport de 225 kV du réseau interconnecté de Libreville ont été réalisés, ouvrant la voie à une nouvelle phase d'essais techniques. L'opération constitue un préalable indispensable à la mise en service de cette infrastructure, dont la puissance installée est de 35 MW. Selon Phillipe Jr Ossoucah, le directeur général de Gabon Power Company, les premières injections sont attendues en décembre 2026. «On escompte déjà avoir les premières injections d'ici le mois de décembre et avoir les 35 MW sur le réseau avant la fin de cette année» , a-t-il indiqué. Des vérifications avant la mise sous tension Les essais, initialement réalisés individuellement sur les équipements du poste électrique, entrent désormais dans une phase globale. L'objectif est de vérifier le fonctionnement de l'ensemble des installations avant leur mise sous tension. Du côté d'Asokh Energy, maître d'ouvrage du projet, la coordination des équipes de Sinohydro et des différents intervenants techniques a été déterminante. Un ingénieur indépendant a également été mobilisé pour contrôler les raccordements et les tests réalisés, condition préalable à l'autorisation de remise sous tension. Cette étape intervient après les perturbations électriques qui ont affecté le Grand Libreville durant les travaux de raccordement. La mise hors tension temporaire de la ligne 225 kV avait réduit la puissance disponible des barrages de Tchimbélé et de Kinguélé. À terme, les 35 MW supplémentaires doivent contribuer à renforcer la capacité de production et à améliorer la desserte de la capitale. Le véritable enjeu sera toutefois de convertir cette nouvelle puissance en une fourniture d'électricité plus régulière pour les ménages et les entreprises. L’article Kinguélé Aval : le raccordement achevé, 35 MW attendus sur le réseau électrique en décembre est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Après l’introduction en bourse, les fondateurs et employés d’Anthropic sont plus riches que 57 pays réunis
items.description: Le laboratoire d’IA américain Anthropic a été introduit en bourse hier, jeudi 19 novembre, à un prix de 83 dollars par action. Porté par l’engouement suscité par l’IPO, le prix a dépassé la fourchette envisagée (70 à 78 dollars) : l’action a clôturé à 97,17 dollars (soit +17 % par rapport au prix d’introduction), et l’entreprise a terminé la journée avec une valorisation d’environ 1 760 milliards de dollars sur une base entièrement diluée, en comptant les options et actions attribuées. L’opération a contribué à l’une des créations de richesse les plus conséquentes et les plus rapides de l’histoire pour les fondateurs et employés de l’entreprise, fondée il y a moins de six ans. Selon une estimation de la revue, la valeur des parts des sept cofondateurs d’Anthropic s’établit à 23,2 milliards de dollars en moyenne après l’introduction en bourse, et 163 milliards de dollars collectivement. Les 5 300 employés de l’entreprise, via leurs options d’achat d’actions et leurs actions gratuites (dont une partie n’est pas encore acquise), détiennent quant à eux en moyenne environ 51 millions de dollars. Le classement des milliardaires de Bloomberg place au 19 novembre les sept cofondateurs de l’entreprise entre la 100e et la 106e place des personnes les plus riches au monde, juste derrière Peter Thiel (24,4 milliards de dollars) et peu après Greg Brockman (25,5 milliards), le président d’OpenAI, mais devant le patron américain des médias Rupert Murdoch (19,8 milliards) et sa famille. L’introduction en bourse d’Anthropic bouscule également la répartition des richesses aux États-Unis. Selon l’analyste américain Steven Rattner, ancien conseiller de l’administration Obama, les 433 milliards de dollars d’actions et d’options détenus par les fondateurs et employés d’Anthropic équivalent au patrimoine cumulé du tiers des foyers américains les moins fortunés, soit environ 45 millions de foyers. Anthropic's 5,300 founders and employees are now worth more than the bottom third of U.S. households (45 million families). pic.twitter.com/mmaCblgQlQ — Steve Rattner (@SteveRattner) November 19, 2026 Si les 5 300 employés détiennent en moyenne environ 51 millions de dollars, plus de 400 salariés devraient voir leur fortune dépasser les 100 millions de dollars, et plusieurs d’entre eux pourraient même devenir milliardaires Anthropic IPO will create thousands of multimillionaire employees », CNBC , 19 novembre 2026.'> 1 . Selon Jasmine Sun, l’une des voix les plus influentes de la Silicon Valley, cette richesse générée occupe une place secondaire pour nombre d’employés d’Anthropic : leurs discussions sur l’introduction en bourse portent surtout sur la manière de répartir leurs actions, désormais liquides, dans leurs comptes de dons caritatifs I Spent a Year Talking to Anthropic Employees. Here’s What They Believe. », The New York Times , 18 novembre 2026.'> 2 . Peu d’entre eux prévoient de vendre leurs actions juste après l’introduction en bourse, la plupart s’attendant à ce que leur valeur augmente. L’article Après l’introduction en bourse, les fondateurs et employés d’Anthropic sont plus riches que 57 pays réunis est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Bilawal wants PM Shehbaz to become first premier to complete 5-year term
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Friday that he wanted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to become the first premier to complete a five-year term in office. Since the country came into being in 1947, no elected prime minister has ever completed their five-year term. Addressing an event in Karachi, Bilawal, citing the economic crisis resulting from the US-Israeli war on Iran, called for “empowering” PM Shehbaz so that he could present a way forward to tackle the crisis. “My objective is that I want to strengthen the hand of the prime minister [..] usually politicians create difficulties or plot his fall and secure the seat for themselves. I will not do that […] I am saying that I want Shehbaz Sharif to be the first prime minister […] to complete a five-year term,” Bilawal said. Bilawal noted that the prime minister had not been “given the chance” to focus on the economic issues so far. “What can he do? Whenever he [PM Shehbaz] makes a plan, some federal minister objects and presents their own agenda to divert the topic at hand.” The PPP chairman insisted he wanted the premier to complete his term as he foresaw difficulties ahead for the country. “I am saying this because I know that there is no consideration for the people of Pakistan. Whether one province is created or a 1,000, the only worry the public has is having access to meals twice a day,” Bilawal said, recalling his party’s slogan of ‘ roti, kapra, makan’ as primary concerns for the public. Bilawal reiterated that the premier’s “hand should be strengthened” so he can draw attention to the economic issues facing the country. In that regard, he also underscored the need for a “national effort”. “While I am praying for the success of the prime minister, I also believe that if we are to face the real issues of the country, one or two political parties alone cannot achieve this. It has to be a national effort,” Bilawal said. He added that it did not matter whether the government “liked” Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman or PTI founder Imran Khan, who Bilawal said had President Asif Ali Zardari and his sister Faryal Talpur “imprisoned.” Bilawal asserted that he would not do politics “based on ego and personal vendettas” as he believed that it was not “more important than national interest”. He called on the government to engage the opposition, particularly the PTI, in dealing with the country’s issues. “My political differences with Khan sahib and his own mistakes aside, his party still has a majority representation in the opposition. And if we have to face these issues collectively then we will have to engage them, entice them and request them to play their role in [parliamentary] committees,” the PPP chairman said. Bilawal added that the PPP would continue to work as per its “ideology and others may follow suit should they wish”. “We cannot force someone, but it is my right to present my stance, and it is the prime minister’s right to decide whether he wants to take into account my suggestion,” he said. Bilawal claimed that the PPP’s sole focus was to draw attention to the public’s grievances and expressed the hope to succeed in doing so. The development comes amid renewed tensions between coalition partners, the PPP and the PML-N, triggered by a hard-hitting speech delivered earlier this week by Bilawal. In the no-holds-barred address, Bilawal had warned against new provinces, constitutional tweaks, criticised the treatment of the opposition and past decisions taken by the ruling coalition. Bilawal had also warned against “political revenge” in politics. “What a weird country this is; since 1947, whoever becomes the prime minister goes to jail, whoever gets out of jail goes to sit in the Prime Minister’s House,” he remarked. The PPP chairman had referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s recommendation of holding a referendum to decide on the creation of new administrative units and said: “In our history, a referendum has always been carried out for an undemocratic act and never a democratic one.” He also remarked that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse” — seemingly reacting to Naqvi’s statement in July that the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. In the aftermath, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and other leaders from the ruling PML-N criticised the Bhutto scion for his remarks. Despite this, Bilawal went on a media blitz on Wednesday, articulating the PPP’s grouse with the federal government and questioned many of its past decisions. This led to PM Shehbaz and Naqvi going to meet his father, President Asif Ali Zardari. According to the brief official readout issued by the Presidency, the three men reviewed the current political situation, and resolved that all pending issues would be resolved through dialogue and discussion. While leaders from both parties remained tight-lipped over what transpired during the meeting, observers termed it an attempt at ‘damage control’ or ‘mending fences’ after Bilawal adopted a decidedly aggressive tone against the ruling PML-N.

items.title: Mahama targets 50,000 National Apprenticeship Programme beneficiaries in 2027 as over 13,000 graduate
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to expand the National Apprenticeship Programme to cover at least 50,000 young people in 2027, following the graduation of more than 13,000 beneficiaries from its maiden cohort. The expansion, according to the President, will mark a transition from the programme’s pilot phase to a larger-scale training initiative aimed at equipping more young Ghanaians with practical skills and improving their prospects for employment and entrepreneurship. The announcement was made at the maiden National Graduation Ceremony of the programme, where President Mahama reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to technical and vocational skills development as a means of addressing youth unemployment and strengthening the country’s workforce. The graduating beneficiaries have undergone training in several fields, including fashion and textiles, beauty and personal care, craftsmanship and artisanal trades, hospitality and tourism, and agriculture and agro-processing. President Mahama said the government was preparing to increase the programme’s capacity significantly, with a target of training at least 50,000 apprentices in the next phase. “Next year, we are going to train at least 50,000 apprentices,” he announced. He explained that the initial phase had involved approximately 14,000 young people, describing it as a pilot exercise ahead of the broader implementation planned for 2027. GH¢1bn expected from CST to support youth programmes To support the planned expansion, President Mahama disclosed that he had directed the Minister of Finance to uncap the Communication Service Tax (CST), a move he said would generate an additional GH¢1 billion for government programmes. “I asked the Minister of Finance to uncap the Communication Service Tax. And by uncapping the Communication Service Tax, it releases an extra GH¢1 billion,” he said. He indicated that the expected revenue would be channelled into several youth-focused interventions, including the National Apprenticeship Programme, the Adwumawura Programme and initiatives under the Youth Employment Agency (YEA). The President said the additional funding would help the government extend skills training opportunities to more young people while providing support for those seeking to establish their own businesses. The proposed expansion is expected to increase access to practical vocational training across different sectors, particularly for young people who may not have opportunities to pursue conventional academic pathways. President Mahama also encouraged beneficiaries interested in setting up their own businesses to take advantage of the Adwumawura Programme, which is designed to provide start-up support for young entrepreneurs. He described the initiative as a natural next step for apprenticeship graduates who intend to turn their newly acquired skills into sustainable business ventures. “For those of you who have graduated from the National Apprenticeship, for those who want to set up their own businesses, the next module you should be looking at is the Adwumawura Programme,” he told the graduates. “You’ll get the start-up capital to establish your business and become an entrepreneur.” The President’s appeal highlights the government’s intention to connect vocational training with business development, ensuring that beneficiaries have opportunities to move beyond acquiring skills into establishing enterprises. Beyond expanding access to apprenticeship training, President Mahama called for greater participation of women in technical and traditionally male-dominated professions. He rejected the notion that certain occupations should be reserved for men, insisting that women had the ability to excel in every field when given equal opportunities. “Let us not say some professions are reserved for males. Every profession, what a male can do, a female can do even better,” he stressed. He urged young women entering the labour market to consider opportunities in technical and industrial trades rather than allow traditional perceptions to restrict their career choices. He said increasing women’s participation in such professions would broaden the country’s skilled workforce and create more opportunities for economic advancement. With the government targeting at least 50,000 apprentices in 2027, the next phase is expected to significantly widen the programme’s reach. However, the success of the expansion will also depend on the availability of adequate funding, effective training arrangements and opportunities for graduates to apply their skills in the labour market. The proposed collaboration between the National Apprenticeship Programme and the Adwumawura initiative is expected to provide an additional route for beneficiaries seeking to establish businesses and become self-employed.

items.title: Espagne | Libération du sponsor du Club africain Fergie Chambers
items.description: La justice espagnole a officiellement remis en liberté provisoire le sponsor américain du Club Africain, Fergie Chambers. Selon le journal espagnol El Diario, cette remise en liberté provisoire est assortie de la confiscation de son passeport, de l’interdiction de quitter le territoire espagnol et de l’obligation de se présenter au tribunal chaque lundi. L’homme d’affaires a maille à partir avec la justice des Etats-Unis, qui avait émis une demande d’extradition en son nom. Il restera donc soumis à cette procédure jusqu’à la décision finale de la justice espagnole concernant son extradition. Fergie Chambers a hérité d’une partie de la fortune de son père et utilise ces fonds pour financer des causes communistes et révolutionnaires, notamment en soutenant des mouvements tels que Stop Cop City à Atlanta ou des collectifs pro-palestiniens. En 2023, il a fondé les «Berkshire Communists» , un collectif marxiste-léniniste basé dans le Massachusetts, où il ouvre également une salle de sport réservée aux militants anticapitalistes. Pour ne rien arranger, cet homme qui s’est marié trois fois et a quatre enfants s’est converti à l’islam après s’être marié avec une sportive tunisienne. Tout cela, on l’imagine, ne cadre pas avec l’ordre américain des choses. I. B. L’article Espagne | Libération du sponsor du Club africain Fergie Chambers est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: DR Congo: The Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak in Africa: Six-Month Situation and Response Report
items.description: Countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda Source: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Executive summary This report examines the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak and the continental response from the declaration on 15 May 2026 to the evidence available for preparation of the six-month milestone on 15 November. It integrates pathogen and transmission knowledge, zoonotic origin and One Health, epidemiology, clinical care, operational performance, country experiences, research, financing, logistics, essential health services, social consequences and preparedness. The principal finding is that substantial response capacity was mobilized, but persistent transmission and mortality indicate that this capacity did not consistently translate into sufficiently early detection, timely access to care, complete identification of transmission networks and reliable local service delivery in DRC. The introduction that began the outbreak also remains unexplained, so the risk of further spillover in the affected landscape persists independently of progress against human-to-human transmission. Key findings that should guide the next phase 1. The burden remains overwhelmingly concentrated in the DRC. Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria provide distinct experiences of managing cross-border or travel-associated infection. Their outcomes should be assessed against their own case histories and observation periods. France’s imported case and medical evacuations to other countries belong in a separate international account so that the same patient is not counted twice. 2. Early growth was exceptional, but historical comparison requires matched definitions. The early reported burden substantially exceeded burden observed during the comparable early periods of major 2014 and 2018 Ebola epidemics, although direct quantitative comparison is constrained by differences in case categories included, uncertainties in disease onset and official detection and declaration, ascertainment and observation intervals. Historical comparisons should therefore preserve the original case classifications and reporting periods. 3. Contact tracing misses most new cases: Only 11% of confirmed cases (1,146 of 10,659 with onset from week 19 to week 45) came from the contact lists, against a target of 95%. The response found the other 89% outside those lists, which means many transmission links were identified too late to list and monitor the contacts. The daily contact follow-up [text continues beyond the visible page]. Five headline numbers in the analytical snapshot By 8 November 2026, five countries had reported 11,021 confirmed cases and 5,358 deaths, a crude case-fatality ratio (CFR) of 48.6%. The DRC carries almost all of this burden, with 10,990 cases and 5,354 deaths (CFR 48.7%). Uganda reported 20 cases and 2 deaths, Kenya 9 and 2, Nigeria 1 imported case and no deaths, and France 1 imported case and no deaths. In the DRC, 67 health zones in eight provinces have reported at least one confirmed case, and 51 of 67 health zones reported a case in the last 21 days. National notifications have held at about 460 to 480 confirmed cases a week since late September; the epidemic is a sustained plateau and not yet declining.

items.title: Chefferies locales : un nouveau cadre pour les désignations
items.description: © Internet Le texte ratifié jeudi accorde une place plus nette aux coutumes dans le choix des chefs. Il précise aussi leurs obligations et le fonctionnement des conseils qui les entourent. Le Conseil national de transition a ratifié, le 19 novembre, l’ordonnance du 11 août 2026 portant statut des villages, fractions et quartiers. Les 121 membres présents ont voté en faveur du texte. Ce vote achève l’examen parlementaire d’une réforme engagée plusieurs mois plus tôt. Dans de nombreuses localités, la désignation d’un chef peut faire naître des désaccords entre familles et conseillers sur la coutume à appliquer. Le gouvernement a présenté ces blocages répétés, ainsi que la politisation de certaines chefferies, parmi les raisons de la réforme. Les règles de désignation et de service des chefs et de leurs conseillers sont désormais rattachées aux coutumes et traditions établies dans chaque localité. Le texte affirme en même temps l’obligation d’impartialité des chefs et précise les incompatibilités liées à leur fonction. Il supprime le mandat des conseils de village, de fraction et de quartier, sans supprimer ces conseils. Une indemnité de fonction est prévue pour les chefs, ainsi qu’une part des recettes de la taxe de développement régional et local effectivement recouvrées avec leur concours. Ces dispositions concernent les conditions d’exercice de la fonction, pas seulement les cérémonies de nomination. La réforme touche aussi la vie des familles. Elle formalise le cahier de recensement, registre à partir duquel sont délivrés les carnets de famille. Elle précise les procédures de transfert ou de changement de nom d’un village, d’une fraction ou d’un quartier. Pour les habitants, l’application de ces règles se verra autant dans les démarches auprès des autorités locales que lors des prochaines désignations.

items.title: Trafic de véhicules volés: 2 394 engins saisis et 688 suspects arrêtés dans 65 pays
items.description: L’opération internationale Carback II, menée du 28 septembre au 9 octobre 2026 avec la participation du Burkina Faso et de 64 autres pays, a permis l’arrestation de 688 suspects et la saisie de 2 394 véhicules volés. Dans un rapport publié ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026, INTERPOL fait également état du démantèlement de 30 groupes criminels organisés et révèle les connexions du trafic automobile avec d’autres formes de criminalité transnationale. Le trafic international de véhicules volés est une activité criminelle qui alimente bien d’autres formes de délinquance. C’est ce que met en évidence l’opération Carback II, dont les résultats ont été rendus publics ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 par l’Organisation internationale de police criminelle (INTERPOL). Menée avec le soutien de l’Agence européenne de garde-frontières et de garde-côtes (Frontex), cette vaste opération a mobilisé les forces de l’ordre de 65 pays, dont le Burkina Faso, et abouti à 688 arrestations ainsi qu’à la saisie de 2 394 véhicules. Au cours de cette opération, qui s’est déroulée du 28 septembre au 9 octobre 2026, les autorités ont également récupéré 1 891 pièces de véhicules et saisi des drogues illicites, de l’argent liquide et des armes. Trente organisations criminelles ont été démantelées, tandis que plusieurs autres font encore l’objet d’investigations. Pour parvenir à ces résultats, les forces de sécurité ont renforcé les contrôles des véhicules, des passagers et des marchandises dans des zones préalablement identifiées comme des points sensibles du trafic automobile. Plus de 1,5 million de consultations ont été effectuées dans les bases de données d’INTERPOL, donnant lieu à 1 180 résultats positifs. Parmi ces vérifications figuraient plus de 480 000 recherches sur les immatriculations de véhicules dans la base de données internationale des véhicules volés. Pour David Caunter, directeur de la criminalité organisée et émergente à INTERPOL, le phénomène dépasse largement la simple atteinte aux biens. «Le crime avec la route est bien plus qu’une infraction à la propriété», a-t-il souligné, expliquant que les véhicules volés constituent à la fois une source de revenus pour les réseaux criminels et un moyen de faciliter d’autres activités illicites. Ils peuvent notamment être revendus, servir de monnaie d’échange entre groupes criminels ou être utilisés pour transporter de la drogue, des armes et des marchandises de contrebande à travers les frontières. Des ramifications au-delà du vol automobile Les différentes interventions menées dans le cadre de Carback II illustrent cette imbrication des activités criminelles. En Grèce, la police aux frontières a notamment intercepté trois individus circulant à bord de véhicules équipés de plaques d’immatriculation françaises valides. Des soupçons sur leur comportement ont conduit à la vérification des documents d’enregistrement, qui se sont révélés falsifiés. La coopération avec les autorités françaises a permis d’établir que les véhicules avaient été loués et que les suspects tentaient de les faire sortir de l’Union européenne avant que les sociétés de location ne signalent leur détournement. En Argentine, près de 360 composants automobiles, dont des boîtes de vitesses, des disques de frein et des blocs moteurs, ont été saisis, portant un coup au commerce illicite de pièces détachées. Au Nicaragua, les policiers ont démantelé un réseau spécialisé dans le vol de motos louées, à l’aide de faux actes de vente et de signatures falsifiées. Les engins étaient ensuite revendus ou mis en gage. En Allemagne, l’interception d’un véhicule portant des plaques d’immatriculation volées a permis de remonter jusqu’à un réseau présumé de trafic de migrants. Une fouille a conduit à la découverte d’un bateau gonflable et d’un moteur de bateau volé. L’exploitation du téléphone du conducteur a ensuite révélé l’implication de ce dernier et de son passager dans ce réseau. Les deux suspects ont été détenus. D’autres interventions ont également mis au jour des liens avec des crimes violents. Au Venezuela, des dizaines de véhicules associés à des enquêtes portant notamment sur le trafic de drogue, les vols à main armée et les homicides ont été saisis. En Côte d’Ivoire, les opérations ont abouti à deux arrestations et à la saisie de drogues, de médicaments illicites, d’argent et de biens volés. Une coopération internationale décisive La coordination entre les pays a également joué un rôle déterminant dans la localisation de véhicules volés. Deux unités de coordination opérationnelle ont été mises en place, l’une au bureau régional d’INTERPOL à Buenos Aires et l’autre au centre de coordination mobile 9 des Journées d’action conjointes de Frontex, à Varsovie. Ces dispositifs ont permis un échange continu de renseignements et un suivi en temps réel des opérations. Grâce aux données GPS et aux informations partagées, plusieurs véhicules ont ainsi été retrouvés au-delà de leurs pays d’origine. En Mauritanie, les agents ont récupéré une Toyota volée en France. Au Sénégal et au Nigeria, les autorités ont retrouvé deux voitures volées au Portugal. En Bolivie, un véhicule dérobé en Argentine a également été localisé et saisi. Par ailleurs, des renseignements transmis par les douanes canadiennes ont permis d’intercepter, au port de Tanger, deux véhicules haut de gamme volés au Canada alors qu’ils étaient en transit. En parallèle, l’opération JAD Mobile 9, conduite par Frontex en Europe, a permis la saisie de 710 véhicules supplémentaires et 334 arrestations. Menées de manière complémentaire, les deux initiatives ont ainsi renforcé la capacité des services de sécurité à lutter contre les réseaux transfrontaliers. Au-delà des 2 394 véhicules récupérés, Carback II met surtout en évidence l’ampleur des ramifications du trafic automobile dans la criminalité organisée internationale. Financée par le gouvernement canadien à travers le projet Drive Out, cette opération confirme l’importance du partage de renseignements et de la coopération entre États pour remonter les filières criminelles et s’attaquer aux réseaux qui les alimentent. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Trafic de véhicules volés: 2 394 engins saisis et 688 suspects arrêtés dans 65 pays est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Settling disputes
items.description: WITH almost 2m court cases clogging the lower judiciary — most of them in Punjab — Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s nod to a proposed panchayat system to resolve local-level disputes is expected to be well received by many litigants. Several factors are responsible for a situation in which disputing parties often find themselves waiting for decades before their cases are settled. A shortage of judges , unclear rules, frequent court adjournments, and corruption at all tiers are just a few of the underlying causes. It is no wonder then that informal forums of ‘justice’, based more on centuries-old, often barbaric customs than on modern legal principles, persist in the country. Seen in this light, a panchayat system that prioritises community decision-making but with some state regulation, appears, at least theoretically, to be the right move. However, as with any initiative, it is important to closely study similar local justice schemes elsewhere before embarking on the proposed project. For instance, India’s village justice court system aimed at providing inexpensive and accessible justice to rural communities in the country, has had mixed results that should provide a useful clue for the government here. In fact, Pakistan is no stranger to alternative dispute resolution laws intended to reduce the burden on the courts. The Punjab Alternative Dispute Resolution Act, 2019 — recently repealed by the Punjab Alternative Dispute Resolution Ordinance, 2026 — is a case in point. The ‘success’ of the repealed law can justifiably be questioned. How will the proposed panchayat framework ensure better results? It is too early to be ambitious. Small steps towards the larger goal of an integrated justice system will allow the authorities to ensure accessible legal relief for Pakistan’s rural communities — measures that are sensitive to local concerns without straying from constitutional norms. Above all, there can be no further dillydallying on reforms that strengthen the judicial system — judicial slots must be filled, procedures simplified, and corruption reined in. Published in Dawn, November 20th, 2026

items.title: On North Waziristan visit, CDF Munir vows to eliminate terrorism, preserve peace in KP
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir reaffirmed on Friday the security force’s “unwavering resolve” to decisively eliminate terrorism and preserve peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in close coordination with law enforcement agencies (LEAs). The CDF said this during a visit to Miranshah in KP’s North Waziristan, the military media wing said in a statement. “He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the Security Forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the statement by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) quoted him as saying. He also appreciated the “brave police force” in KP and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter terrorism efforts and ensure lasting peace and stability in the area”, the ISPR statement said. It added that CDF Munir also interacted with officers and troops and appreciated their “high level of preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment to the defence and security of the motherland”. Upon his arrival in Miranshah, the CDF was received by the Peshawar Corps commander and later laid a floral wreath at Yadgar-i-Shuhada to pay homage to the “supreme sacrifices of the shuhada (martyrs) of the Pakistan Army”, the statement said. His visit to Miranshah comes a day after he visited Turbat in Balochistan, where, too, he was briefed on the prevailing security environment, operational preparedness and ongoing operations against externally sponsored terrorism. Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan. State-run Radio Pakistan reported on Friday that security forces had foiled an attempt by Fitna al Khawarij terrorists to escape disguised as women in Mir Ali, North Waziristan. “The terrorists, who were attempting to flee in a rickshaw while disguised as women, were neutralised,” the report said. On Saturday, ISPR said four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in IBOs in Balochistan and KP’s North Waziristan. Furthermore, last week, 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan. Meanwhile, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring conflict and security developments, has reported encouraging trends in the two provinces in its monthly assessment for October. Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37 per cent, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57pc, and injuries decreasing by 71pc compared to September, the report said. It added that the improvement was particularly pronounced in Balochistan and mainland KP. “Balochistan recorded a substantial reduction in militant violence, with attacks declining by 46pc, from 132 in September to 71 in October. Deaths resulting from militant attacks decreased from 136 to 44, a reduction of approximately 68pc, while injuries declined from 63 to 37, representing a decrease of 41pc,” the report said. Regarding mainland KP, it said a “significant decline” was witnessed in terrorism. PICSS recorded 40 attacks during October, compared with 58 in September, representing a reduction of 31pc. Meanwhile, deaths resulting from these attacks declined from 90 to 38, a decrease of approximately 58pc, while injuries fell from 165 to 19, representing a reduction of 88pc. The merged districts of KP recorded 30 attacks during October, compared with 34 in September, and deaths resulting from these attacks decreased from 33 to 25, while injuries increased from 11 to 13, the report said. In October, the federal government also imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP, citing the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.
